stories.title: MP tourism has no weather alert system for cruise boats:Bhaskar reveals major lapses, false claims in Jabalpur boat tragedy
stories.summary: A probe into the Bargi Dam cruise accident in Jabalpur has exposed major lapses by the Tourism Department. A Dainik Bhaskar investigation found that the cruise was operating without insurance, as the policy had been issued only in the name of Mekal Resort. The department also allegedly failed to inform the insurer that the resort operated a passenger cruise service. The investigation further revealed there was no mechanism to communicate weather alerts to the pilot and crew. Weather monitoring was left entirely to the pilot. Despite a weather alert issued on April 30, the cruise continued operations, even as similar services in Varanasi were suspended over the warning. Passengers were not given any emergency or safety briefing. The state government has ordered an inquiry into the lapses. Taking suo motu cognisance, the High Court directed authorities to register an FIR and submit a report within two days. Ahead of the official findings, Bhaskar’s report details the alleged negligence at multiple levels. The responsibility of monitoring weather lies entirely with the pilot. Despite the alert on April 30, the cruise was operated, whereas operations were stopped in Varanasi for the same reason. Passengers were not given emergency or safety instructions. The government has ordered an inquiry into these negligence. The High Court has taken suo motu cognizance and directed registration of an FIR and submission of a report within two days. Before the investigation report, Bhaskar is revealing at what level the negligence occurred. Read the report..... Know about these lies in detail 1. The Biggest Lie: Insurance in the name of resort, no mention of cruise Tourism Department's Water Activity Head Retired Naval Commander Rajendra Nigam claimed that the cruise insurance was expiring on March 21 and the premium was sent on March 19, which was not approved by the company. What is the truth?: Officials of United India Insurance Company stated that the department had not taken insurance in the name of the cruise at all. The policy was in the name of 'Maikal Resort'. The department also did not inform the company that the resort operates a cruise and that passengers board it. The resort's insurance expired on March 21. On March 24, the department sent a premium of Rs 37,003. Upon learning about the cruise operation, the company returned the money on April 2. According to the company, 'Marine Category' insurance is mandatory for cruises, which requires registration and valuation, but the department did not provide this. The cruise was illegally operated by taking insurance for the resort under the 'Public Liability Insurance Act 1991'. 2. Warning ignored: 41 lives at stake for Rs 8,000 On the day of the accident, the Meteorological Department had issued a 'Yellow Alert' 24 hours in advance and a 'Now Cast' warning 3 hours before about a storm with rain at 60 km per hour. MP Tourism has no system to relay this alert to the pilot. For a ticket collection of Rs 8800 at Rs 220 per person, the lives of 41 passengers were put at risk. Captain Mahesh Patel admitted that he does not receive weather information and operates the cruise based on guesswork. Varanasi showed wisdom On April 29, 721 people had made bookings for cruises in Varanasi. After the weather department's warning, all tickets were cancelled and money was refunded. Here, 7 cruises operate for Ganga Darshan, which have a capacity of 70 to 110 people. Ajay, operator of Vishwanath Cruise, said that bookings were cancelled on the 29th due to the forecast of strong winds. Cruises and boats are prohibited when winds exceed 25 km per hour. 3. Safety and rescue 'system fail' According to rules, wearing life jackets is mandatory for every passenger, but in Bargi they were taken into the middle of the water without jackets. When the cruise started sinking, attempts were made to get the jackets out, but it was too late. Captain Mahesh Patel said that when water started filling in and one engine stopped, he called for help, but the rescue boat did not arrive on time. At that time, the manager of Mackal Resort was in Jabalpur. That means there was no backup plan. 4. Attempt to destroy evidence? cruise dismantled before investigation Serious questions are being raised about the dismantling of the cruise after the accident. There are allegations that it was hastily destroyed to hide poor structure and technical flaws. However, the department argues that it was necessary to rescue people trapped in the cabin. Straight Talk: Rajendra Nigam, Water Activity Head, MP Tourism Question: What do you consider to be the cause of the accident? Answer: This is completely a natural disaster. In 17 years, none of our boats have had an accident. If there had been negligence, there would have been an accident earlier as well. Question: Why did water fill in the cruise? Answer: There was a cyclone that day and the wind speed was so high that the rear part of the cruise stopped working and it capsized. Technically the cruise was fit, it had been repaired in July 2024 itself. Question: Why wasn't the weather department's warning seen? Answer: The staff has been given training. The skipper is qualified. A system for local warnings is now being developed. I could not see that day's warning. Question: Why was the cruise broken? Answer: Our priority was to save people. The cruise had capsized and it was not possible to reach some parts, so it had to be broken.

stories.title: Storms and rain in 8 districts, including Lucknow:Alert Issued for 44 districts, western UP under cloudy skies; people get relief from heat
stories.summary: The spell of storms and rain continues in UP on Thursday morning, when it rained in Lucknow and Pratapgarh. Strong winds had been blowing since late night. Clouds were overcast. At dawn, a storm began and then the rain started. Even now, clouds are covering the sky and there is intermittent drizzling. The cold is being felt due to the light wind. The speed of vehicles on the roads has slowed down. Storms and heavy rain in Lucknow and surrounding areas Meanwhile, the Meteorological Department has issued an alert for storms and heavy rain in Lucknow and surrounding areas for the next 3 hours. In the alert sent on mobile phones, it has been said that winds can blow at a speed of 50 to 70 km per hour along with lightning. During this time, there will be heavy rain. Everyone should remain alert. Go out of the house only if necessary. Relief from scorching heat Actually, the weather has been bad in the state for the past 7 days. Due to storms and rain, the maximum temperature has come down below 40C. The Meteorological Department says that the weather has changed due to western disturbance and snowfall in the mountains. Today, that is Thursday, there is an alert for storms and rain in 44 districts. Talking about the last 24 hours, Banda remained the hottest in the state with a maximum temperature of 38 degrees Celsius. Meanwhile, Bijnor had the coldest night with 16 degrees. Lucknow's meteorological scientist Atul Singh said- Clouds are forming due to the active Western Disturbance over North India. Moisture-laden winds coming from the Bay of Bengal and dry winds coming from the west are colliding with each other, making the atmosphere unstable. The weather will deteriorate today. From tomorrow there will be some improvement in it. Heat will show its intensity again. Weather Pictures- What will the weather be like for the next 5 days?

stories.title: Hamirpur boat tragedy:Rescue ops continue in Yamuna on Day 2; 'please bring back my child,' mother pleads, 5 bodies recovered
stories.summary: A boat overturned in the Yamuna River in Hamirpur district on Wednesday evening, carrying nine people, including eight children. The boatman managed to save three people, but six others, one woman and five children, drowned. By Thursday afternoon, five bodies had been recovered, while one child remains missing, and search operations are still underway. A massive rescue operation involving NDRF and Flood PAC teams with around 100 personnel is continuing. Officials said the river’s depth is making diving difficult, so boats are being moved in circular motion in hopes that water pressure may bring bodies to the surface. A net-based search operation is also being planned. Relatives of the victims are sitting at the riverbank, with one grieving mother pleading with officials to bring back her child. The accident occurred around 6 PM on Wednesday, and rescue operations had to be halted at night due to rain and strong winds. Operations resumed at 6 AM on Thursday with multiple boats deployed. Victims identified, one child still missing The recovered bodies have been identified as Brijrani (25), and children Archana (14), Rani (9), Lavyansh (5), and Aakanksha (9). Eleven-year-old Aditya is still missing. See photos 5 km search operation underway NDRF and SDRF teams are conducting a 5-km search operation using boats. Divers are not entering the water due to the extreme depth. Boats are being rotated in circles to create pressure waves in hopes of surfacing submerged bodies. Authorities are also preparing to deploy nets in the river to prevent bodies from drifting further downstream and to aid recovery efforts. How the accident happened The incident took place in Kutubpur Patiya under Kurara police station in Bhaulee village panchayat, located along the Yamuna River. A wedding had taken place on Tuesday in the village. On Wednesday evening, after the bride’s farewell, nine people including boatman Dheeru crossed the river by boat to visit relatives on the other side. After eating watermelon and cucumber, they were returning when the boat lost balance in the river and capsized. The boat was being operated by Dheeru, who managed to rescue three people, but six others drowned.

stories.title: Woman pushes friend’s son into canal, kills him:35-year friendship ends in murder, took boy on scooter ride in Saharanpur
stories.summary: A woman in Saharanpur has been arrested for allegedly murdering her friend’s 14-year-old son following a dispute over ₹6 lakh, police said. On May 1, she reportedly lured the boy who was outside his house, onto her scooter on the pretext of taking him for a ride. She then took him about 8 km away to a canal and pushed him in. When the child did not return, his family began searching and later filed a missing person report. During the investigation, CCTV footage showed the woman taking the boy on her scooter. Police arrested her the same day, and she confessed to the crime. The boy’s body was recovered from the canal on Saturday. The incident falls under the City police station area. See 3 pictures- Read the complete story of a 15-year friendship turning sour and murder Bal Krishna Bharti lives with his family in the Numaish Camp area. The family consists of his wife Jyoti and 4 sons - Anurag, Vishal, Vikas, and Anshuman (14). Anurag was the eldest, and Anshuman was the youngest. In their neighborhood, a woman named Pooja (42) lives alone in her house. She is a 35-year-old friend of Bal Krishna's wife. According to the police, both families used to visit each other's homes. Pooja had recently sold one of her shops to Jyoti's eldest son, Anurag, for ₹6 lakhs. It was agreed that the money would be paid later. After a few days, a dispute started between them over the money. Pooja alleges that Jyoti and her family members were not paying the money. There was also a quarrel between them over this. Then communication between them stopped. Pooja was very angry about this. She plotted revenge. On May 1, she saw Jyoti's son, Anshuman, roaming around. She called him over, made him sit on her scooter, took him away, and killed him. Woman seen taking child on scooter in CCTV When Anshuman did not return home for a long time, the family became suspicious. They filed a complaint with the police. When police checked nearby CCTV footage, a woman was seen taking Anshuman away on a scooter. The family identified the woman as Pooja. After this, the police took her into custody from her home. Child's body found floating in canal after 2 days When police interrogated her strictly, Pooja revealed that she had pushed the child into the canal. On Saturday, a rescue operation was conducted in the main canal based on her identification. Two divers searched throughout the day, but the child could not be located. On Sunday, passersby near the canal saw the child's body floating in the water and informed the police. Upon receiving the information, the police reached the spot. Anshuman's family members were also called, who identified the body. The police have sent the body for a post-mortem. Accused woman said- I got scared During police interrogation, Pooja said that I had no such intention. I just got scared because his family members were calling repeatedly. They were asking about Anshuman. I panicked because of this. His mother and brother also used to fight with me often. I had no enmity with him. Brother alleges revenge over past dispute The victim’s elder brother, Anurag, said his 14-year-old brother Anshuman went missing from Chhota Chowk on May 1 at 2:04 PM, and his body was found the next morning. He alleged that the accused, Pooja, took revenge for a dispute that took place about one and a half years ago. He said Pooja used to visit their house and had earlier behaved aggressively with the children, which the family had opposed. According to him, she had even threatened to “teach them a lesson,” and has now carried out that threat. He demanded strict justice in the case. Councillor flags misleading statements by accused Councillor Rahul Jham said he was informed by a local resident that a woman named Pooja had taken the child. During questioning, her responses appeared suspicious as she kept giving different locations, including Sarasawa, Yamunanagar, and Thanabhawan. He said the accused misled the police throughout the night, but during strict interrogation, she confessed that on the evening of May 1, around 8 PM, she pushed the child into a canal. He demanded strict action, calling such individuals a threat to society. Police detail investigation and recovery SP City Vyom Bindal said a missing person complaint was received from the Numaish Camp area, after which a case was registered, and a search operation began. CCTV footage showed a woman taking the child away, helping police identify and trace the accused through surveillance. During questioning, the woman confessed to throwing the child into a canal on Ambala Road. A team of over 17 divers was deployed, and the canal flow was temporarily stopped. After nearly 17 hours of effort, the body was recovered on Saturday morning around 6 AM. Police said the accused and the victim’s family had known each other for about 10 years, but had been in dispute for the past one and a half years over financial dealings related to a shop. Investigators believe the murder was carried out as an act of revenge.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:IRGC says, 'Trump left with limited choices'; Yogi announces 1.5 lakh recruitments in UP this year more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news updates from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top headlines: 1. IRGC says Trump left with limited choices A Very Large Crude Carrier (VLCC) owned by National Iranian Tanker Company has reportedly evaded a US Navy blockade and reached the Asia-Pacific region carrying over 1.9 million barrels of crude oil worth nearly $220 million. 2. Yogi announces 1.5 lakh recruitments in UP this year UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Sunday announced that 1.5 lakh recruitments will be carried out in the state within a year. Speaking in Lucknow, he said the Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission (UPSSSC) alone will conduct around 32,000 recruitments, while the Education Selection Commission will also hire thousands of teachers. 3. Air Force rescues 2 children using MI-17 Helicopter, 5 children climbed water tank In Siddharthnagar, Uttar Pradesh, children who were stranded on a water tank for 16 hours were rescued by the Air Force using an MI-17 helicopter. Both were admitted to the Air Force hospital in Gorakhpur. On Saturday, 5 children climbed a 60-foot-high water tank in the Kashiram Awas Colony to make a reel. While getting down, the ladder broke. 3 children fell down. 4. Suvendu Adhikari alleges leak of counting duty details The Election Commission has ordered fresh polling across all 285 polling booths of the Falta assembly seat of South 24 Parganas of West Bengal on May 21. BJP leader and Bengal's LoP Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday alleged that several officers deployed for counting day duties are reportedly disclosing their duty details, locations and designations to their departmental organisations and associations, terming it a serious breach of election protocol. 5. Soil mound collapse in Kaushambi kills 3, 2 rescued A sudden collapse of a mud mound in Kaushambi at around 7 am on Sunday left 5 people buried under debris. In the accident, three people, including a mother and daughter, died on the spot. Police and administrative officials rushed to the site after receiving information and launched a rescue operation. 6. IAS officer Rinku Singh still awaits posting after withdrawing resignation Uttar Pradesh cadre IAS officer Rinku Singh Rahi has not received a posting even 13 days after withdrawing his resignation on April 20, raising questions over administrative delays. The 2021-batch officer said he is willing to serve anywhere but does not feel comfortable drawing a salary without work. 7. Massive fire in Delhi's Shahadara building leaves 9 dead A fire broke out in a 4-storey building in Vivek Vihar, Shahdara of New Delhi, resulting in the death of nine people on Sunday. So far, 3-4 bodies have been found. And around 15 people have been rescued, including two who suffered minor injuries. 8. Woman climbs water tank, threatens to commit suicide A 32-year-old woman, Pallavi Singh, climbed a 50-foot-high water tank in Prayagraj on Saturday around 1 PM and threatened to end her life. From the top, she shouted that a case registered against her was false and said she would not come down until it was withdrawn. 9. Content creators build ₹50,000 crore digital economy Shivani Kumari from Auraiya became viral after she mistakenly said ‘Hello Frenda’ instead of ‘Hello Friend’ in a video. Her unique speaking style became her identity. Today, her net worth runs into crores. Then there is Shadab Jakati from Meerut, who once worked as a driver in Saudi Arabia. He became famous with a simple video asking, “How much is the Rs 10 biscuit, sir?” 10. Mittal family buys Rajasthan Royals in ₹15,660 cr deal Industrialists Lakshmi N. Mittal and Aditya Mittal have agreed to acquire Rajasthan Royals with Adar Poonawalla as partner, valuing the franchise at $1.65 billion (₹15,660).

stories.title: Construction of 108 accommodations begins in PAC:Subedar Nayak performs Bhoomi Pujan; officials say personnel will get better facilities
stories.summary: The construction work of 108 special type residences at the 37th Battalion PAC located in Shyamnagar, Kanpur, was inaugurated. Deputy Commandant Tanu Upadhyay (ADSP) formally commenced this project by performing Bhoomi Pujan with Vedic chanting. This initiative has been taken towards providing better residential arrangements for the battalion personnel and expanding basic facilities. Under the direction of Commandant B.B. Chaurasia, a groundbreaking and Panchshila Pujan ceremony was organized for the 'construction of Special Type First residences'. Officers and staff present on this occasion expressed happiness at the commencement of the construction work. They said that the new residences would provide better residential facilities to the battalion's officers and staff, which would have a positive impact on their work performance. After the Pujan ceremony, prasad was distributed among all present officers, staff members, and representatives of the executing agency (UPPPCL). Under the leadership of Commandant B.B. Chaurasia, continuous development and construction work are being carried out in the 37th Battalion PAC. Officers stated that work is progressing in a planned manner for the all-round development of the battalion premises, so that personnel can receive modern and better facilities in the future. The Bhoomi Pujan (ground-breaking) ceremony was attended by Chandreshwar (Camp Pal), Manoj Kumar Srivastava (RTC In-charge), Arvindra Kumar (Squad Leader G Squad), Ravendra Singh Chaudhary (Subedar Military Assistant), Shivangshu Dwivedi (SQM), Vineet Tripathi (Head Clerk), along with all officers and staff of the battalion. The program was conducted in a peaceful and dignified atmosphere.

stories.title: History-sheeter beaten to death in Fatehpur:8 people attack with sticks and rods; parents were also harmed despite repeated pleas
stories.summary: A 32-year-old history-sheeter was beaten to death with sticks and clubs in Fatehpur. The video of the incident surfaced on Sunday. In the video, 8 people can be seen beating history-sheeter Abhimanyu alias Kunnu Yadav with sticks and clubs. His mother and father are trying to save him. They kept pleading before the accused, but the accused did not listen to them at all. Rather, they beat them, too. The accused fled, thinking he was dead. He died during treatment at the district hospital. The history-sheeter's parents were also injured in the attack. The entire incident took place on Friday in the Husainganj police station area, 10 km from the city. On Saturday, the police handed over the body to the family after the post-mortem. His last rites were performed in the late evening. Police investigation revealed that the history-sheeter had an ongoing dispute with gangster Kamlesh Yadav from the same village. There had been several fights between the two over dominance in the past as well. In this same rivalry, Kamlesh Yadav carried out the incident along with his family members. The police have registered a case against 10 people, including Kamlesh Yadav. History-sheeter was sitting outside the house, beaten with sticks and clubs History-sheeter Abhimanyu was a resident of Poore Rahimal Majra Jamrawan village under Husainganj police station. On Friday morning at 10 o'clock, he was sitting at the door of his house. Just then, Kamlesh Yadav came with his family members carrying sticks and clubs. Seeing them, Abhimanyu tried to run away, but they caught him. They started beating him with kicks, punches, and sticks. When the blood-soaked Abhimanyu raised an alarm, his father, Maan Singh Yadav, and mother, Nanki Devi, came running to save him. When they tried to save their son, they were also beaten, and the accused left after threatening them. The family members took the injured to the district hospital, where Abhimanyu died during treatment. Uncle Gyan Singh Yadav alleged that Kamlesh Yadav, Manish, and Sachin from the village beat his nephew Abhimanyu to death due to an old rivalry. History-sheeter had 20 to 25 cases registered against him SP Abhimanyu Manglik said in the initial investigation that Kunnu Yadav was a history-sheeter of the police station. 20 to 25 cases were registered against him. Cases are also registered against his brother and father. Kunnu Yadav's mental condition was not stable. A notice was sent to the family from the police station regarding this. The notice stated that your son's mental condition is not stable. He used to quarrel frequently, which posed a threat to peace in the area. He had been advised to be admitted to a mental hospital. A day before the incident, on Thursday, Kunnu Yadav had a dispute with the accused. After this, the accused carried out the crime. A video of the murder has surfaced. Based on this, the accused will be arrested as soon as possible.

stories.title: Protests against smart meters spread across 5 UP cities:Residents allege inflated bills, power cuts despite payments; AAP workers clash with Lucknow police
stories.summary: Opposition to smart meters is growing in UP. On Sunday, protests regarding smart meters took place in Agra, Prayagraj, Kanpur, Lucknow, and Varanasi. In Agra, women uprooted smart meters from their homes and threw them on the streets. They said, "We don't want smart meters, we want the old meters. Since the installation of smart meters, electricity bills have been higher. Money is being deposited in advance. Even after depositing money, electricity is being cut. When inquired, they say the balance is in minus''. A protest had also taken place here 2 days ago. Scuffle with police in Lucknow, dragged away The AAP party held a strong protest. AAP workers reached Shakti Bhawan carrying posters and placards in their hands in Lucknow. They started moving towards the Assembly while raising slogans against the BJP government. The police stopped the protesters near Shriram Tower. The protesters insisted on moving forward. This led to a sharp confrontation with the police. The police took them into custody. They were dragged and put into vehicles and taken to Eco Garden. Pratipal Singh, who participated in the protest, has alleged that his turban was pulled off to humiliate him. AAP spokesperson in Varanasi said - We will continue to protest Aam Aadmi Party protested against smart meters at Chaukaghat electricity substation in Varanasi. Spokesperson Mukesh Singh said that common people are being harassed by smart meters. We will continue to protest against it at all costs. Because its bill is being taken arbitrarily. The government should stop it immediately, because it is smartly cheating people. Why is there opposition to smart meters? Read on Electricity consumers say that smart meters run very fast. This results in higher bills even with less usage. Sometimes the balance decreases even without usage. As soon as the balance goes into minus, the electricity supply is cut off. Even after a recharge, the supply is often not restored immediately. After months of opposition to smart meters, the state government issued a new order. According to this, it was stated that electricity would not be cut off for connections up to 1 kilowatt for 30 days, and for 2 kilowatt connections, even if the balance goes minus by ₹200.

stories.title: 1.5 lakh recruitments in UP this year, says Yogi Adityanath:Teachers, 45,000 home guards, inspectors to be hired
stories.summary: UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Sunday announced that 1.5 lakh recruitments will be carried out in the state within a year. Speaking in Lucknow, he said the Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission (UPSSSC) alone will conduct around 32,000 recruitments, while the Education Selection Commission will also hire thousands of teachers. He added that the Public Service Commission will provide about 15,000 jobs. The UP Police Recruitment and Promotion Board is currently recruiting 45,000 Home Guards and Sub-Inspectors, with a similar number of vacancies expected in the near future. Overall, around 1.5 lakh appointments will be made in 2026–27 through various commissions and boards. During the event, CM Yogi distributed appointment letters to 357 Junior Analysts (Medicine) and 252 Dental Hygienists selected by UPSSSC. He also took a swipe at past practices, alleging that earlier recruitment processes were marred by corruption. He said that officials and influential figures used to engage in extortion, and stressed that it is everyone’s responsibility to stand against dishonest leaders and bureaucrats. CM narrated the story of a youth's suicide due to not getting a job The Chief Minister said he recalled an incident from his time as an MP from Gorakhpur. One evening, a highway was blocked after a young man died by suicide. The area fell within his constituency, and officials advised him not to visit due to public anger, but he chose to go. He said that when people saw him, the situation calmed down. He spoke to the crowd and met the bereaved family. During his inquiry, he was told that the young man had secured a general rank in a police recruitment process but did not receive an appointment letter, which led him into depression and, eventually, to take his own life. Read Yogi's 4 big statements- 1- We have a law of life imprisonment for those who breach recruitment The CM said that a strict law has been made to ensure that no recruitment process is breached. Whoever is found guilty of fraud in recruitment, there is also a law to confiscate their property and sentence them to life imprisonment. Parents wish that their sons and daughters get a good education and a good job, but when expected results don't come, and a young person's dreams are shattered, it is not just a betrayal of that youth, but also a betrayal of the future of the coming generation. UP didn't become a BIMARU state just like that. Through discrimination and corruption in the selection process, the state was turned into a BIMARU and anarchic state. The state was plagued by hooliganism. Curfews would remain in place for months. There was discrimination in the selection process. Courts had to stop recruitments. Someone else would take the exam, and someone else would receive the appointment letter. 2- Earlier, everything was left to God; today, there are 81 medical colleges The CM said that if we leave aside four or five districts, almost all of the 75 districts in the state have medical colleges. Today, there are 81 medical colleges and two AIIMS. Earlier, there were neither colleges nor staff. Everything was left to God. Results also came accordingly. People didn't even know about the Food Safety and Drug Administration. What medicine they were taking, whether it had quality or not, there was no inspection of this. There was adulteration in everything. Who would stop it? The police could hardly stop it. The responsible department didn't have labs. Test results would take years to come. Adulterators couldn't be punished. Adulteration in milk, spices, fruits, and sweets was common. The department responsible for this work had neither adequate staff, nor labs, nor equipment. Now labs have been established at the division level for testing samples. They have equipment and manpower available. Food safety-related samples can be tested in the same commissionerate. 3- Earlier people were only concerned about their own and their family's health The Chief Minister said that now test samples are examined within a fixed time, and people are informed whether they are correct or not. Earlier, there were only five laboratories, but now 18 well-equipped labs are operational. The number of samples has increased from 12,000 earlier to 55,000 now. He added that earlier, people did not fully understand the importance of health and focused only on themselves and their families. Emphasising dental care, he said that if a tooth is damaged, it affects the taste of food. With better dental doctors now available, people will receive proper guidance, leading to improved health. 4- A lot has changed in 9 years Yogi said that significant changes have taken place over the last 9 years. He remarked that earlier, even ineligible individuals, including those with fake degrees, became commission chairpersons and oversaw recruitments, often involving corruption. As a result, recruitment processes were stalled. After his government came to power, he questioned why police recruitments were not happening and found that several cases were pending in courts. He said the process was then completed in accordance with court directions, and so far, 2.20 lakh recruitments have been made in the police department. He added that earlier the scale of work was limited, but things have changed. In 2025, when 60,244 police constables were recruited at once, many doubted whether UP could handle their training. However, the entire training was conducted within the state, and the candidates have since been deployed. Earlier, only about 3,000 constables could be trained at a time in the state.

stories.title: Groom spends 20 years’ savings on elephant wedding entry:Hires ‘royal elephant’ for ₹2.6 lakh; says dream matters, rich or poor
stories.summary: A young man from Meerut fulfilled a childhood dream by arriving at his wedding procession on an elephant instead of the traditional mare. Ankit had dreamed of this since the age of five and had shared it with his father and grandfather. Taking his wish seriously, the family ensured that his dream would come true. On April 21, Ankit’s wedding procession travelled from Jamalpur to Mandaura village with him seated on an elephant. Before heading to the bride’s village, Ankit rode through his own village on the elephant. The unique sight drew large crowds, with villagers gathering to watch the unusual procession. The wedding, from Jamalpur village under Inchauli police station area, has since become a talking point in the region. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Ankit said, “A dream is a dream. Whether one is rich or poor, everyone has the right to fulfil it. My dream was to bring my bride home while riding an elephant, and today it has come true.” First, see these pictures... Read the complete conversation with Ankit and his father... A family living in a hut-like house Ankit's father name is Kalu. There are a total of 6 children in the family, including 4 daughters and 2 sons. Ankit lives with his family in Jamalpur village. Their house is a kutcha (temporary structure). Many rooms don't even have a roof. The entire family lives in the open in a hut-like house. Ankit's father works as a laborer. Ankit also works cutting sugarcane in fields and doing labor work. He gets a daily wage of about ₹500 rupees. The family's expenses are managed with this. He has done ITI after 12th standard. He has recently given the Railway exam. He is also preparing for several other competitive examinations. First got younger siblings married Ankit said that I never took away my siblings' rights for my dreams. First, I got my younger brother married. He had a love marriage. He has three children and lives separately. My two elder sisters are also married. Now, I live with my grandfather, father, mother, and two younger sisters. Only after the marriage of two sisters and my younger brother did I think about my own marriage, so that there would be no pressure on anyone. The relationship happened with family consent Ankit said that my dream was to take out the wedding procession riding on an elephant. To fulfill this desire, I invested all my savings. My marriage is with Pooja, who lives in Mandaura village of Muzaffarnagar. This is an arranged marriage. We also got an elephant's picture printed on the wedding card, which made people quite excited. When I reached the girl's village with the wedding procession riding on an elephant, the people there also liked my style very much. Elephant came from Rajasthan for two and a half lakh rupees Ankit said that we wanted a royal elephant as we needed. It was not available in Meerut or nearby. On asking people, we found out that good elephants are available in Jaipur, Rajasthan. After that, we searched on Google. We got the number of Imran Bhai from Jaipur, who provides elephants for weddings. We booked the elephant online and called it to Meerut. The elephant's rent and travel expenses were around ₹1 lakh 60 thousand. It cost approximately ₹1 lakh for the permission to bring the elephant from Rajasthan to Meerut. Thus, the total expenditure came to ₹2 lakh 60 thousand. The company people themselves brought the food items for the elephant. They had specified some things for the elephant, which we arranged here. Now, my wife and I, and the entire family, are very happy. Elephant brought from Rajasthan in a truck The elephant reached Ankit's house from Rajasthan on April 21 at around 2 PM. It was brought in a truck. After reaching home, a ceremony was held in the village. Ankit, dressed as a groom with a turban on his head and a sword in his hand, rode the elephant. The elephant was taken around the entire village. After this, the elephant was taken by truck to Mandaura village in Muzaffarnagar. Outside the village, Ankit again sat on the elephant and reached the bride's house with the wedding procession. There too, people appeared quite excited seeing the elephant. After the wedding rituals, at around 2 AM at night, the elephant was sent back from Muzaffarnagar to Jaipur by truck itself. Father say happy that son's wish was fulfilled Ankit's father, Kalu, said, "My son had decided in his childhood that he would sit on an elephant as a groom. That's when we also resolved that his wedding procession would go on an elephant, no matter what it takes." "Ankit and I saved for about 20 years for this. We worked hard and did labor to collect this amount. With that money, we called an elephant and took the wedding procession with my son sitting on the elephant. Today I am happy that we could fulfill his dream." Such a sight seen after 75 years In old times, there was a tradition among the elite of taking out wedding processions on elephants. According to local people, such a sight was seen in the area after about 75 years, when a groom took out a wedding procession riding on an elephant. It is said that before this, in the year 1951, the wedding procession of Delhi resident Niranjan Gupta had come to Lavad. At that time, too, the groom had arrived with the wedding procession riding on an elephant.

stories.title: Woman climbs water tank, threatens to commit suicide:Claims case against her is false; refuses to come down until withdrawn
stories.summary: A 32-year-old woman, Pallavi Singh, climbed a 50-foot-high water tank in Prayagraj on Saturday around 1 PM and threatened to end her life. From the top, she shouted that a case registered against her was false and said she would not come down until it was withdrawn. As her voice drew attention, hundreds of people gathered at the spot. Police reached the scene and tried to persuade her to come down, assuring her that appropriate action would be taken after an investigation. Pallavi remained atop the tank for nearly 9 hours, creating a tense situation. She finally came down around 10 PM, after which the police took her to the station. The incident took place in the Phaphamau area, about 15 km from the city. During the investigation, police found that Pallavi had a love marriage with Mohammad Alam. Her husband had filed a fraud case against her at the Phaphamau police station, following which Pallavi also lodged a case against him. See 3 pictures of the girl's drama... A day before, a picture with notes had surfaced Pallavi Singh is originally a resident of Ballia. She currently lives in Phaphamau. A day before, her picture had surfaced on social media, in which she was lying on a bed covered with ₹500-500 rupee notes and using her mobile phone. On Saturday at one o'clock in the afternoon, she climbed up a 50-foot-high water tank built near Basna drain in Phaphamau. People present there thought that the young woman had gone to talk on the phone. But eyewitnesses said that the girl broke the lock of the ladder and went up. After this, a crowd gathered there. Meanwhile, a passerby woman climbed up the tank to counsel the young woman. But the young woman started a Facebook live. The young woman said that I have become a victim of love jihad, I have consumed poison. The police filed a case against me. Don't motivate me, go away from here. After this, she drove the woman away, threatening to jump. 'Theft is being orchestrated at my house daily' Coming live on Facebook, the young woman Pallavi made serious allegations against the Phaphamau Inspector. She said that Alam (husband), a relative of Atiq Ahmad, along with other people, files cases against me every day. I have been greatly harassed by the Prayagraj administration; I have no option left except suicide. Theft is being orchestrated at my house daily, to the extent that the Phaphamau Inspector himself broke into my house and committed theft in 2024. ACP Tharwai reached the spot after 1 hour About 1 hour later, at 2 PM, ACP Tharwai reached the spot and tried to bring her down by calling out through a microphone. Around 3 PM, he himself climbed onto the tank to persuade the young woman, but even after hours of convincing, she did not come down. Meanwhile, the young woman was continuously live on Facebook and was also talking on a call from another phone. The young woman shouted from above and said that the crowd should be removed from here, and a case should be registered against my husband, Alam, and he should be sent to jail. Even after this, the ACP kept trying to persuade her. She kept threatening to jump and end her life. Finally, around 10 PM at night, after getting assurance that all her conditions would be met, she somehow came down with the ACP. Station House Officer Kambod Singh informed - Several cases are already registered against Pallavi in different police stations. She is being interrogated regarding the picture that surfaced with the currency notes.

stories.title: Soldier kills wife at girlfriend's behest:Befriends 11 years younger girl on Facebook; says, ‘Kill her if you want to be with me’
stories.summary: A soldier killed his wife for his girlfriend in Bareilly. Police revealed that the soldier used to give ₹15k every month to his girlfriend, whom he met on Facebook, to support her expenses. However, when the girlfriend found out that the soldier was married, a fight started between them. After this, the girlfriend told the soldier that if you want to stay with me, you will have to kill your wife. Blinded by love, the soldier strangled his wife to death on April 22 at his girlfriend's behest. After the incident, the soldier called and told his girlfriend everything. Based on CCTV and call details, police arrested the girlfriend on May 1. On the same day, the accused soldier surrendered in court. The case is from the Subhash Nagar police station area. CCTV footage that revealed the secret Now read the entire matter in detail sequentially.... Met on Facebook 5 years ago Originally a resident of Badaun, Bharat Singh (35) was living in Geeta Colony, Bareilly. He had built a house here a year ago. Bharat Singh Yadav was posted in the army in Firozpur, Punjab. 16 years ago, Bharat Singh married Geeta Yadav (32). They have two children, Drishya (14) and Harsh (12). Both children study in the Army School. About 5 years ago, Bharat Singh met Surbhi Yadav (24), a resident of Badaun, on Facebook. Bharat introduced himself as a bachelor. The two became friends, and gradually this friendship turned into love. The two started talking for hours on the phone. Bharat started sending ₹14-15k to Surbhi every month. However, when Surbhi came to know that Bharat was married and had two children, disputes started between them. Called girlfriend after the murder During this time, Surbhi laid down a condition that if he wanted to live with her, he would have to kill his wife. Only after that would he be able to live with her. On April 18, Bharat Singh took leave and reached Badaun. There, both of them together decided that Geeta should be murdered so that they could get married. On the night of April 21, Bharat left from Surbhi's place and reached Bareilly around 4:00 AM on April 22. At 11:15 AM during the day, he came to his house. With a towel tied around his face and holding an umbrella in his hand, he entered the house so that his identity could be hidden. Geeta was alone at home, and both children had gone to school. Bharat brutally strangled Geeta to death and fled from the scene. After the murder, he immediately called Surbhi and informed her about it. However, the entire incident was captured on CCTV camera. Secret revealed through CCTV and call details Accused tried to hide his identity, but the children recognized him from his walk in the CCTV footage. After this, the police intensified the investigation based on call details and surveillance. On May 1, the police arrested Surbhi Yadav, while Bharat Singh surrendered in court. Used to beat mother daily The son, Drishya, revealed that there were frequent fights between mom and dad. Dad used to talk to a girl. When mom would forbid him from doing so, dad would beat her. A day before the murder, Dad had called and said that you must go to school tomorrow. The son said with a choked voice that if I had even the slightest idea that Dad would kill Mom, I would have never gone to school that day. Drishya revealed that her dad had been hiding in Bareilly for several days, but had lied at home that he was on duty. Deceived the unit too in the name of leave The investigation revealed that Bharat Singh had taken leave from his unit starting April 17 by showing a fake wedding card. He told his family he was in Jammu, while he was actually staying in Bareilly. SP City Manush Pareek stated- Based on CCTV and surveillance, suspicion deepened on the accused husband. The investigation revealed the girlfriend's role in the murder conspiracy, after which she has been arrested. The main accused will be taken on remand for further action.

stories.title: Air Force rescues 2 children using MI-17 Helicopter:5 children climbed water tank to shoot reel; 3 fell after ladder collapsed, 1 dead
stories.summary: In Siddharthnagar, Uttar Pradesh, children who were stranded on a water tank for 16 hours were rescued by the Air Force using an MI-17 helicopter. Both were admitted to the Air Force hospital in Gorakhpur. On Saturday, 5 children climbed a 60-foot-high water tank in the Kashiram Awas Colony to make a reel. While getting down, the ladder broke. 3 children fell down. Out of these, 1 died, while 2 are in critical condition. 2 children hung onto rods and then slowly climbed back onto the tank. Due to the marshy area around the tank, difficulties were faced in the rescue operation. A hydraulic crane was called, but it could not reach the tank due to the swamp. Therefore, work to build a 150-meter road was started. By late night, about 120 meters of the road had been constructed. Meanwhile, around 3 am, heavy rain started, forcing the work to stop. Considering the situation, the administration sought help from the army. After this, on Sunday morning at around 5:20 am, an Air Force MI-17 helicopter reached the spot. Both children were rescued safely. First, understand the entire incident in a sequential manner… In the Kashiram Awas Colony located at the district headquarters, Bale (12), a resident of Mohana, had come to his maternal cousin Deepchand’s house. On Saturday, around 3 pm, he, along with Golu (15), Shani (11), Kallu (15), and Pawan (16) from the neighborhood, climbed a dilapidated water tank near the housing colony to make a reel. After staying on top for a while, all of them started coming down one by one. Suddenly, after descending just four steps, the dilapidated ladder broke. As a result, Bale, Shani, and Golu fell down. Debris from the ladder fell on Bale, causing his death on the spot. Shani and Golu were injured. Kallu and Pawan got stranded on top. After the incident, chaos broke out at the spot. Nearby people rushed to the scene. In a hurry, people carried the injured in their arms and took them to the hospital, where doctors declared Bale dead. After receiving information, DM Shivsharanappa GN and SSP Abhishek Mahajan, along with several officials, reached the spot. Relief and rescue operations were initiated. A poclain machine was called to clear the debris.

stories.summary: A sudden collapse of a mud mound in Kaushambi at around 7 am on Sunday left 5 people buried under debris. In the accident, three people, including a mother and daughter, died on the spot. Police and administrative officials rushed to the site after receiving information and launched a rescue operation. The accident took place while soil was being excavated from a pond. Suddenly, a large mound of mud caved in and came crashing down, trapping those working below it. Panic spread instantly, with screams heard across the area. Local residents rushed to help, triggering scenes of chaos and urgency. Villagers and police are jointly carrying out rescue efforts and pulling out the injured from under the debris. They are being shifted to a nearby hospital for treatment. The deceased have been identified as Uttara Devi, Geeta Devi and Bitti. The bodies have been taken into custody and sent for post-mortem. stories.title: Creators turn crorepatis by making videos online:Build ₹50,000-crore digital economy; earnings go up to ₹4.5 lakh a month
stories.summary: Shivani Kumari from Auraiya became viral after she mistakenly said ‘Hello Frenda’ instead of ‘Hello Friend’ in a video. Her unique speaking style became her identity. Today, her net worth runs into crores. Then there is Shadab Jakati from Meerut, who once worked as a driver in Saudi Arabia. He became famous with a simple video asking, “How much is the Rs 10 biscuit, sir?” The clip went so viral that rapper Badshah and cricketer Rinku Singh made videos on the same theme. These are just two names. Uttar Pradesh now has thousands of content creators whose lives have been transformed by social media. Many of them would have struggled to secure jobs paying even Rs 10,000 to Rs 20,000 a month. Today, by making videos, they are earning between Rs 4 lakh and Rs 4.5 lakh every month. Estimates suggest that the social media content business in UP alone has grown into a Rs 50,000-crore annual industry, while across India, it is now worth nearly Rs 3 lakh crore. In today’s Sunday Big Story, here is a look at how creators earn from video content, how ordinary people are becoming celebrities, and what different social media platforms offer. Became a hit with the slipper video, today a millionaire Shivani’s journey as a content creator is remarkable. She once worked as a farm labourer. In 2018, while going to the market to buy slippers for her sister’s children, she made a video and accidentally said ‘Hello Frenda’. The video went massively viral on TikTok, and by 2020, Shivani had gained 50 lakh followers. After TikTok was banned, she shifted to Instagram, YouTube and Facebook. Her first earnings were Rs 20,000. She mainly creates videos around daily life and village routines. When asked whether she can now be called a crorepati, Shivani smiled hesitantly and said, “Yes… you can say that now.” Kapil is promoting several brands in IPL Kapil Kanpuriya from Kanpur, whose real name is Kapil Shukla, once went to Mumbai hoping to become an actor. After failing there, he returned and took up an accountant’s job in Gurugram in 2017. When the lockdown began in 2020, Kapil started making videos on relatable topics such as how to recover borrowed money and how to complain to a company’s HR department. His content quickly connected with people. He later brought his mother Pushpa and wife Kirti into his videos. Family-based content made him hugely popular, and today several companies approach him for brand promotions. During the IPL, Kapil was seen promoting multiple brands. His monthly earnings have now reached lakhs. Rapper Badshah, cricketer Rinku Singh among many celebrities following Shadab, from Inchauli town in Meerut, had worked as a driver in Saudi Arabia. After returning to UP, he shot a video at a local shop on 15 May 2025, asking: “How much is the Rs 10 biscuit, sir?” The video exploded online, drawing 89 million views on Instagram. His theme was later copied by celebrities including rapper Badshah and cricketer Rinku Singh. Today, companies in Delhi, Meerut and Ghaziabad regularly approach Shadab for promotions, paying him lakhs of rupees. Recently, he even opened a jewellery showroom in Meerut. Though controversies have also surrounded his name, his popularity remains high. Jackie Yadav from Etawah has 4 lakh followers on X. He earns nearly Rs 2 lakh every month from X alone, apart from brand promotion income. Jackie said, “I was preparing for UPSC CSE till 2021. In 2022, I started writing on political and social issues through my account. By the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, more than one crore people were reading me every day.” He added, “People now see me as a trendsetter. I currently have a team of three people helping with research. My name featured in the Top-20 ranking list related to X. With social media earnings, I bought a Thar and a Brezza.” How Can You Earn from Different Platforms? YouTube Channel Need 1,000 X (formerly Twitter) You can get 2000 to 3000 rupees for one million views Social media platform X, earlier known as Twitter, was bought by Elon Musk on 27 October 2022 for 44 billion dollars. From July 2023, X introduced payouts for creators. To qualify, creators need X Premium, which costs Rs 472 a month, and gives a blue tick. To become eligible for payouts, an account must achieve: Once eligible, creators can earn 25 to 30 dollars per one million views. However, X payouts depend heavily on how many verified users engage with your post. X pays every 14 days. If during that period your account records: then earnings can touch 150 dollars. Content Creator Economy Will Reach $1 Lakh Crore A big question remains—how many content creators are there in India? At the WAVES Summit in Mumbai in May 2025, it was stated that India has 20 to 25 lakh creators with more than 1,000 followers. A Boston Consulting Group report says only 8 to 10% of content creators are currently making money—roughly 2 lakh to 2.5 lakh people. The rest either earn very little or are still trying to monetise their content. In March 2025, Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said: “We will create a 100-crore-dollar arrangement for the creator economy.” Social Media Platforms Make the Real Money It is also worth noting that in 2025, YouTube earned Rs 34,742 crore from India, while Meta, through Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, earned nearly Rs 29,392 crore. Creators may be making money—but the biggest profits are still flowing to social media companies.

stories.title: IAS who made clerk do sit-ups still awaits posting:Says ‘no calls received’; retired IAS calls it government’s discretion
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh cadre IAS officer Rinku Singh Rahi has not received a posting even 13 days after withdrawing his resignation on April 20, raising questions over administrative delays. The 2021-batch officer said he is willing to serve anywhere but does not feel comfortable drawing a salary without work. Speaking to Bhaskar, Rahi said, “I just want work. Wherever the government posts me, it doesn’t matter. Taking salary without working does not feel right.” Currently, Rahi has been attached to the Revenue Council, headed by Chairman Anil Kumar. Sources said he was recently assigned departmental work by the chairman, which he has completed. However, no formal posting order has been issued so far. No clarity on posting, no calls from officials Rahi said there is still no clarity regarding his role after withdrawing his resignation. “I haven’t demanded any specific posting. I only want to work,” he said, adding that while he received several calls after submitting his resignation, no official has contacted him since he withdrew it. He confirmed that he continues to receive full salary while on attachment but reiterated discomfort over being without responsibilities for nearly nine months. IAS Rinku Singh Rahi on posting delay Question: What process is underway after you withdrew your resignation? Answer: It is not very clear what is happening in my case right now. I have not made any demand for posting; I just want to work. Question: Did you receive a call from any officer? Answer: After submitting my resignation, I received many calls. But after withdrawing it, no officer has contacted me. Question: So are you receiving your salary? Answer: I am on attachment and receiving full salary. Question: You resigned because you were getting salary without work, right? Answer: I have not had any work for the past nine months. That is why taking salary without work does not feel right. I want a posting so that I can do some work. Attachment has no fixed timeline, says retired IAS officer A retired IAS officer said that in such cases, it is entirely the government’s discretion to keep an officer on attachment while awaiting posting orders. There is no fixed timeline for this process. The government may appoint an APO (Assistant Prosecution Officer) if it chooses. However, traditionally, officers are given postings within a few months. Met senior officials, still awaiting posting IAS officer Rinku Singh Rahi has met Chief Secretary SP Goyal, Revenue Council Chairman Anil Kumar, and Additional Chief Secretary (Personnel) M. Devraj. He briefed them about recent developments and requested a posting so he could work for the public. However, no posting has been given so far. Abhishek Prakash case highlights contrast Retired IAS officers point out that Abhishek Prakash, former CEO of Invest UP, was suspended on March 20, 2025, over bribery allegations. After the High Court quashed the chargesheet, he was reinstated on March 14, 2026, and was given a posting the very next day as Secretary in the General Administration Department. IAS officer removed after sit-up controversy 44-year-old Rinku Singh Rahi, a 2021-batch IAS officer, still has around 16 years of service left but has been without a field posting for the past nine months. He was removed from Shahjahanpur and attached to the Revenue Council after a controversy during his tenure as SDM of Puwaiyan tehsil. Rahi earlier served as Joint Magistrate in Mathura before taking charge as SDM in Puwaiyan at 2 pm on July 24, 2025. During an inspection, he noticed Vijay (38), a clerk of a lawyer, using a spot near a wall as a toilet inside the premises. He stopped him and directed him to use proper facilities. The clerk responded that the toilets were dirty. This angered the SDM, who blamed tehsil staff and made the clerk do sit-ups on the spot. At the same time, lawyers were protesting on the premises. When they learned about the incident, they confronted the SDM. Rahi told them the clerk had made a mistake, but the lawyers objected, saying such punishment was inappropriate. They challenged him, asking if he could do sit-ups himself. Rahi replied there was no shame in it and performed five sit-ups. A video of the incident later surfaced, triggering backlash, after which he was removed and attached to the Revenue Council. ‘System needs fixing, not exit’: Rinku Singh Rahi Following the controversy, Rahi wrote to the President on March 26 seeking a technical resignation. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, he clarified that it should not be seen as quitting service but as a request or option. “If I am not being allowed to work in this position, I should be sent back to my original service (PCS),” he said. Rahi was a PCS officer before being inducted into the IAS and now wants to return to the PCS cadre. He maintains that he does not want to leave public service but believes there are systemic shortcomings that need to be addressed. “Some officers leave the system, but I want to stay and improve it,” he said.

stories.title: Western disturbance to turn active after 48 hours:Winds sweep west UP, crops get damaged by rain
stories.summary: Temperatures had dropped across Uttar Pradesh due to rainfall over the past 48 hours, but bright sunshine returned on Saturday, pushing mercury levels up by 2 to 3 degrees Celsius once again. The Meteorological Department has said that another western disturbance is likely to become active in the next 48 hours. Crops damaged by rain, Yogi says - Officers should go to the field Rainfall has caused damage to crops across Uttar Pradesh, with vegetable crops being the worst affected. Farmers fear maximum damage to cucumber, gherkin, muskmelon and watermelon crops. They say continuous moisture after rainfall could cause crops to rot. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has directed officials to provide compensation to farmers affected by rain damage. He has asked officers to go to the fields, carry out an on-ground survey of losses, and submit a report to the government at the earliest so that farmers can receive timely and appropriate compensation. Weather pictures- Rain hits crops again, CM orders immediate ground survey Rain has damaged crops in several districts, especially vegetables. Crops such as cucumber, gherkin, muskmelon and watermelon are feared to have suffered the most. Farmers say excess moisture could lead to rotting. CM Yogi has ordered compensation for affected farmers and directed officials to visit fields, assess the damage and quickly submit their reports so that relief can be provided without delay. In Farrukhabad, it rained for 30 minutes on Thursday night. More than 1,000 sacks of wheat kept in the mandi got soaked. Now know what the meteorologist said According to senior scientist Atul Kumar Singh from the Regional Meteorological Centre, the impact of the outgoing western disturbance has largely ended. Except for isolated light drizzle in some Terai areas, most parts of the state witnessed clear and dry weather on Saturday. He said temperatures are expected to rise by 4 to 6 degrees Celsius before another round of rain begins from May 4 under the influence of a fresh western disturbance, likely bringing thunderstorms and rain across the state. What will the weather be like for the next 5 days? This Year's Rainfall Under the Shadow of El Nino Between June and September this year, Uttar Pradesh, along with the rest of the country, may receive below-normal rainfall. Director General of Meteorology Dr M Mahapatra said signs indicate that La Nina-like conditions in the Pacific Ocean are ending and the system is gradually shifting towards El Nino, which is associated with reduced rainfall. This suggests that this year’s southwest monsoon could remain weaker than normal. He also said reduced snow cover in the Northern Hemisphere between January and March this year may further impact the monsoon. Know About El Nino and La Nina-

stories.title: Maharana Pratap Jayanti rally turns violent in Hapur:Youth pushed from rooftop, cars vandalised; 6 injured
stories.summary: A rally taken out on the birth anniversary of Maharana Pratap turned violent in Uttar Pradesh’s Hapur district on Saturday afternoon. The 5-km-long rally, involving nearly 100 bikes and cars, descended into chaos after an argument broke out between a youth and a shopkeeper in Dehra village of Dhaulana area. According to police, some youths participating in the rally had stopped to garland Maharana Pratap’s statue when one of them went to a nearby shop. An argument started between the youth and the shopkeeper over an issue that soon escalated into a physical altercation. See 4 pictures of the chaos Stone-pelting, rooftop assault leave several injured Police said both sides called their associates to the spot, after which a violent clash erupted. Eyewitnesses claimed heavy stone-pelting took place from both sides, triggering panic and a stampede-like situation in the area. During the violence, 4 to 5 cars were extensively vandalised and windows of several nearby shops were damaged. Amid the commotion, some youths climbed onto rooftops to escape. Locals allegedly chased one youth to a rooftop, pushed him down and assaulted him with kicks and punches. Around 5 to 6 people from both groups were injured in the clash. All injured were admitted to Dhaulana CHC for treatment. Heavy police force deployed, two accused arrested Police personnel deployed for rally security informed senior officers after the situation spiralled out of control. Forces from several police stations rushed to the spot and dispersed the crowd. The disturbance reportedly continued for nearly one-and-a-half hours. Heavy police deployment remains in the area to maintain law and order. Superintendent of Police KG Singh reached the spot and appealed to people to maintain peace. CCTV footage being examined to identify accused Police said CCTV footage from nearby areas is being scanned to identify those involved in the violence. Two accused have been arrested so far. ADG Bhanu Bhaskar said the clash began after a dispute at a shop during the rally procession. “SP KG Singh and I inspected the spot. Two accused have been arrested after calming the situation. Remaining suspects are being identified through CCTV footage and all accused will be arrested soon,” he said.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:Akhilesh promises free education for girls if SP forms govt; VCK extends unconditional support to TVK to form govt more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest updates from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. VCK extends unconditional support to TVK to form government The suspense over government formation in Tamil Nadu ended on Saturday after the Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK) and the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) extended support to TVK chief Vijay, helping the alliance cross the majority mark in the Assembly. 2. Akhilesh promises free education for girls if SP forms govt; responds to Rajbhar’s remark Akhilesh Yadav on Saturday promised free education for girls from KG to PG, free treatment for the poor, and 300 units of free electricity if the Samajwadi Party forms the government in Uttar Pradesh. 3. UP weather machines show faulty flood alerts; ₹137 crore paid to company despite warnings on system faults Faulty weather machines installed across Uttar Pradesh are allegedly showing flood-like rain alerts during light showers and incorrect temperature readings. Despite the Meteorological Department warning that the Hyderabad contractor’s equipment was giving inaccurate data, the Relief Department reportedly paid ₹137 crore, affecting accurate storm and rainfall forecasting. 4. Suvendu becomes Bengal's first BJP CM Suvendu Adhikari became the first BJP Chief Minister of West Bengal on Saturday, taking the oath in Bengali in the name of God. After the ceremony, he approached Prime Minister Narendra Modi and bowed before him. 5. Constable’s live-in partner linked to IPL betting racket in Jhansi; huge cash gold recovered Yashasvi Dwivedi (24), girlfriend of absconding constable Rajat Singh, had appeared for the SI recruitment exam and was living with him in a live-in relationship in Jhansi. Police arrested her and associate Nisha Khan after raiding their flat and recovering gold biscuits, jewellery worth ₹1.55 crore, ₹19 lakh cash, mobiles, and laptops linked to an IPL betting racket allegedly run by BJP leader Ashish Upadhyay. 6. UP gang offers fake rape case in ₹20 lakh:Kingpin says 16-yr-old will get physical with someone else, and another will be framed A fake FIR racket operating across all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh has come under scrutiny after a gang leader was allegedly heard offering to trap people in false rape cases for up to ₹20 lakh. Police sources say the gang includes dozens of girls, many of them educated, who allegedly file fake rape complaints on the gang leader’s instructions. 7. ‘China helped Pakistan during Op Sindoor’ China has publicly acknowledged for the first time that it assisted Pakistan during Operation Sindoor. According to a South China Morning Post report, Zhang Heng, an engineer at the Chengdu Aircraft Design and Research Institute, said that his team was providing technical assistance in Pakistan. 8. 'Leave your parents if you want to live with me’:Husband in Gonda says wife demanded ₹10 lakh despite family selling buffaloes to fund her studies In Gonda, a 5th pass youth worked as a laborer to get his wife to complete a nursing (ANM) course. He says that after getting a job, his wife is not ready to live with him. She is demanding 10 lakh rupees. She says that if you want to live with me, then leave your elderly parents. 9. Father kills his only 13-year-old son, dumped body in pond; stabs himself in neck after being caught A father strangled his 13-year-old only son to death in Greater Noida. He threw the body in a pond by the roadside, away from home. He came home and fabricated a false story that his son had gone missing. Police started the investigation, and when the family checked nearby CCTV footage, the son was last seen with his father. 10. BCCI warns players families to 'Refrain from posting pictures videos' The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has started taking stricter action during IPL 2026 to ensure players, officials, broadcasters, and team members follow anti-corruption guidelines properly.

stories.title: Bulldozers return to Varanasi’s Dalmadi lanes:Around 45 houses razed amid tight security for road widening project
stories.summary: Bulldozers rolled into Varanasi’s Dalmadi area once again on Saturday, as authorities began demolishing around 45 houses under the long-pending road widening project. The entire locality was turned into a heavily guarded zone, with nearly 300 police personnel deployed to prevent any disturbance during the operation. The demolition drive began around 12.30 pm amid tight security arrangements. Barricades were placed across adjoining lanes, restricting movement in one of the city’s busiest commercial stretches. Residents were warned in advance Officials of the Public Works Department had carried out public announcements on Thursday night, asking residents and shopkeepers to remove belongings from their homes and shops before noon on Saturday. Authorities said the operation was part of the ongoing Dalmadi redevelopment and road expansion plan, which has gained pace after Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath recently reviewed the project during his Varanasi visit. The proposed road, currently around 650 metres long, is set to be widened to 17.4 metres. Project covers houses, mosques and shops According to officials, a total of 187 properties were identified for acquisition and demolition. The affected structures include: The first phase of demolition had started on October 29, 2025. What has been demolished so far Before Saturday’s action, nearly 60 houses had already been razed in previous phases of the drive. After the latest operation: Officials indicated that action involving the mosques would be taken only in the final phase of the project. ACP explains ongoing operation ACP Atul Anjan Tripathi said the administration was acting against dilapidated structures and properties already registered with the PWD. He said adequate security arrangements had been made considering the dense population and heavy movement in the Chowk and New Road areas. Police personnel wearing helmets and safety jackets remained stationed across the site through the evening. Debris removal continues till evening Even hours after the demolition began, bulldozer action continued in Dalmadi, with teams engaged in clearing debris from the narrow lanes. PWD teams, backed by heavy machinery and police deployment, continued operations late into the evening as the government pushed ahead with one of Varanasi’s most sensitive urban redevelopment projects.

stories.title: 6 new ministers to join Yogi government:Manoj Pandey gets place, Bhupendra Chaudhary, Surendra Diler and Krishna Paswan also finalised
stories.summary: The Yogi cabinet will be expanded for the second time on Sunday. Six new ministers will take oath at 3:30 pm. MLA Manoj Pandey, who rebelled against the Samajwadi Party, will be made a minister. Apart from him, former state president Bhupendra Chaudhary, Surendra Diler, Krishna Paswan, Hansraj Vishwakarma and Kailash Rajput have also been finalised for the cabinet. Among the new ministers, one is from the Brahmin community, three belong to the OBC category and two are from the Dalit community. Earlier on Saturday evening around 6:30 pm, Chief Minister Yogi met Governor Anandiben Patel. After a discussion of nearly 45 minutes, Yogi handed over the list of new ministers to the Governor. Meanwhile, on Sunday, the Governor and CM Yogi will watch the film ‘Krishnavatram’ at Lok Bhavan. The entire cabinet will also remain present with Yogi. Information regarding this has already been sent to all ministers. At present, the Uttar Pradesh government has a total of 54 ministers, including CM Yogi. The first expansion of Yogi 2.0 took place on March 5, 2024, just before the Lok Sabha elections. 1- Bhupendra Singh Chaudhary: He is the former Uttar Pradesh BJP state president and one of the prominent Jat faces from western Uttar Pradesh. He belongs to Moradabad and has remained active in the RSS and BJP organisation for a long time. He became a Member of the Legislative Council (MLC) for the first time in 2016 and is still an MLC. After the BJP government was formed in 2017, he was made Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Panchayati Raj, and in 2019 he became Cabinet Minister for Panchayati Raj. 2- Manoj Pandey: He is an MLA from the Unchahar Assembly seat in Rae Bareli. He served as a Cabinet Minister in the Samajwadi Party government between 2012 and 2017. In 2022, he was elected MLA on an SP ticket. He also served as the Samajwadi Party’s chief whip in the Assembly. Manoj Pandey is considered a major Brahmin leader in Awadh and eastern Uttar Pradesh. 3- Krishna Paswan: She is a BJP MLA from the Khaga Assembly seat in Fatehpur district. Krishna Paswan, who began her struggle-filled life as an Anganwadi worker, is counted among the prominent Dalit leaders of the district. She has been elected MLA four times and has also served twice as a district panchayat member. She is considered a trusted women’s face of the Uttar Pradesh BJP. 4- Surendra Diler: He is a BJP MLA from the Khair Assembly seat in Aligarh district. He is among the BJP’s prominent young Dalit leaders. He is the son of former BJP MP from Hathras, Rajveer Singh Diler. His grandfather Kishan Lal Diler was elected MLA six times and MP four times. His father Rajveer Singh Diler has also served once as an MP and once as an MLA. 5- Hansraj Vishwakarma: He is a BJP Member of the Legislative Council (MLC). Known for his strong hold in backward class politics, Hansraj Vishwakarma has been active in politics for the last 34 years. He started his political journey at the booth level in 1989. He also played an active role in the Ram Temple movement. He is believed to have played an important role in the BJP’s major victories in Varanasi during the 2019 Lok Sabha elections and the 2022 Assembly elections. 6- Kailash Singh Rajput: He first won the Tirva Assembly seat in 1996 as a BJP candidate. Later, he contested the 2007 election on a BSP ticket and won again. In the 2017 Assembly elections, he rejoined the BJP and returned to the Assembly after winning the election. In 2022 too, he retained victory from the Tirva Assembly seat in Kannauj district. Effort to Address Brahmin Discontent There has been resentment among the Brahmin community over issues such as the Shankaracharya controversy, the new UGC rules, and a controversial question related to the word ‘Pandit’ in the police recruitment examination. According to sources, RSS joint general secretary Arun Kumar had asked the BJP government and organisation, during a coordination meeting, to address the concerns of the Brahmin community. At present, the cabinet has a total of seven Brahmin ministers, including Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak. After former minister Jitin Prasada became an MP and Union minister, one seat from the Brahmin quota in the Yogi cabinet became vacant. For this position, the party has chosen Manoj Pandey, who will take oath on Sunday. Two Ministers from the Dalit Community By including Surendra Diler and Krishna Paswan in the cabinet, the government is trying to send a message to the Dalit community. Earlier, the Yogi government had a total of eight Dalit ministers, including Cabinet Minister Baby Rani Maurya. In the Uttar Pradesh Assembly, a total of 86 seats are reserved, including 84 for Scheduled Castes and 2 for Scheduled Tribes. Out of these, 67 Dalit MLAs belong to the BJP. Know who the ministers are in the Yogi cabinet right now Space Created for Women in the Cabinet The Uttar Pradesh Assembly has 51 women MLAs. Out of these, 30 belong to the BJP, 4 to Apna Dal (S), and 1 to the Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD). At present, the Yogi government has a total of five women ministers. The Constitution Amendment Bill required to implement women’s reservation could not be passed in Parliament. The BJP has been raising this issue against the opposition among women voters. To strengthen this message further, Krishna Paswan has been given a place in the cabinet. From the backward class community, Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya, and Cabinet Ministers Swatantra Dev Singh, Dharampal Singh, Rakesh Sachan, Anil Rajbhar, Dara Singh Chauhan and Chaudhary Laxmi Narayan are part of the cabinet. Among the allies, Cabinet Ministers Ashish Patel, Om Prakash Rajbhar and Sanjay Nishad also belong to the backward class community. Apart from them, there are five Ministers of State with Independent Charge and six Ministers of State from the same category. In Sunday’s cabinet expansion, three leaders from the backward class community have been included. These include former state president Bhupendra Chaudhary from the Jat community, along with Hansraj Vishwakarma and Kailash Rajput. Four ministers were inducted in the first cabinet expansion The first expansion of Yogi 2.0 took place on March 5, 2024, just before the Lok Sabha elections. During that expansion, four leaders were sworn in as ministers. These included SBSP chief Om Prakash Rajbhar, who broke alliance with the Samajwadi Party and joined hands with the BJP, Dara Singh Chauhan, who left the SP and joined the BJP, Anil Kumar from the RLD quota, and BJP leader Sunil Sharma. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav has taken a swipe at the Uttar Pradesh cabinet expansion. He wrote, “Has the slip arrived from Delhi?” He also said that the Chief Minister’s powers were being reduced. Akhilesh further remarked, “At least ask those whose cabinet it is.” He also wrote, “Will they only make reels, or will something good also be done?”
