stories.title: BJP leader, businessman arrested over double murder:Alleged affair between married employee and divorced woman turns fatal
stories.summary: Two murders within 15 days in Baghpat have shocked locals, with both bodies later recovered in Saharanpur. The victims were contractual employee Vikrant and his girlfriend Rakhi. Rakhi, known for carrying a pistol, had been divorced twice and was in a relationship with 42-year-old married Vikrant. The back-to-back killings left people wondering what led to the double murder. Around 15 days after the killings, main accused BJP Yuva Morcha leader Sudharas Chauhan was arrested from Baghpat on May 1 (Friday), revealing the full sequence. Police say the double murder involved a love affair, betrayal, disputes, fear of being caught and political links. Here’s a detailed account of the case and its key characters… Vikrant was originally from Prayagraj and had been working as a contractual employee with DUDA (District Urban Development Agency) in Baghpat since 2018. On April 15, 2026, he reached office, worked as usual and returned in the evening to his rented accommodation in Arjunpuram Colony. When he did not report to office on April 16, his colleagues tried calling him, but his phone was switched off. His family was then informed. Wife filed missing complaint on April 23 Vikrant’s wife Prachi (35) works in the Irrigation and Water Resources Department in Noida. The two were married 10 years ago and have a daughter. Distressed by her husband’s disappearance, Prachi searched for him among relatives. After exhausting all options, she filed a missing complaint on April 23. She raised suspicion about a woman named Rakhi, saying Vikrant was in contact with her and that she was putting pressure on him and threatening him to fulfil her demands. Following this, police swung into action and began their investigation. Rakhi's entry in the case...who was later murdered Based on the missing complaint filed by Vikrant’s wife Prachi, police extracted Rakhi’s mobile call details. It was found that Vikrant had been in frequent contact with Rakhi Kashyap. On April 18, Baghpat police questioned Rakhi. Several questions were asked, but she kept giving evasive answers. Vikrant's body recovered on April 17 On April 17, police in Saharanpur recovered a body from a canal, but it could not be identified. The body was wrapped in cloth, hands and legs were tied, and heavy blows had been inflicted on the head and face to make identification difficult. While Saharanpur and Baghpat police were investigating this unidentified body, another body — of an unidentified woman — was recovered on April 27 from the forests of Naugaon under Mirzapur police station limits. She had been murdered with a sharp weapon and her throat had also been slit. Later, she was identified as Rakhi. After that, the entire case began unfolding layer by layer. Shot fired at party hit Vikrant...body thrown in canal Two arrests have been made in the case so far. Investigation has revealed that on April 16, a party was held at Rakhi’s house in Baghpat. Present at the gathering were Vikrant, Rakhi, Rakhi’s friend and former BJP Yuva Morcha city president Sudharas Chauhan, medicine trader Kapil Chauhan and others. The party was hosted by Sudharas Chauhan. During the gathering, an argument broke out over some issue. The dispute escalated so much that Rakhi allegedly shot Vikrant in the thigh with her licensed pistol. The three panicked. Instead of taking injured Vikrant to hospital, they took him to a deserted place, tied his hands and legs, wrapped him in cloth and dumped him. Later, Rakhi’s body was also found. Her throat had been slit, and she had multiple knife wounds on her chest and back. In Rakhi’s murder case, police have detained Sudharas Chauhan and Kapil Chauhan and questioned them, but police have not yet made an official disclosure. Now read...about Rakhi who lived a luxury life? Police investigation revealed that 27-year-old Rakhi Kashyap was a resident of Rajpur-Khampur village in Baghpat. Her life — marked by a luxury lifestyle, a licensed pistol in hand and expensive tastes — looked glamorous from the outside, but was deeply complicated within. Two marriages — the first in Meerut, the second elsewhere — both ended in divorce. She had no contact with her family for seven years. Living in different places and creating a new identity each time had become part of her life. Rakhi’s father Sherdeen died four years ago. Her elder brother Rajeev runs a chowmein cart, while her younger brother is Vikas. After her divorce, Rakhi first lived in Khekra and later shifted to Arjunpuram Colony in Baghpat. She rented a room there by introducing herself as a contractual worker in DUDA. According to locals and the police probe, Rakhi had disputes with several people and was accused of cheating many. She allegedly trapped people in romantic relationships and extorted money from them. She was also in contact with several influential people, including some political leaders. Her social media account had around 11,000 followers and she had made 1,903 posts. There were posts from Thailand on Instagram. She also made reels while carrying her licensed pistol tucked at her waist. Other posts on her account also mentioned trips to several countries. Rakhi-Vikrant were in a relationship for three years Police investigation revealed that Vikrant and Rakhi had been in a relationship for around three years. Records showed regular phone calls and long conversations between them. The two were even planning to get married. ₹4 lakh withdrawn from account two days earlier Two days before going missing, Vikrant withdrew ₹4 lakh from his bank account. It is being said that in December 2025, Vikrant and Rakhi had a serious dispute over some matter. In anger, Rakhi allegedly set Vikrant’s car on fire. Now know why Rakhi was murdered? According to police, Sudharas Chauhan and Kapil Chauhan — accused in Vikrant’s murder — feared they would be exposed. Rakhi was a crucial link in the entire episode and knew too much. That is why they allegedly planned to eliminate her too. Rakhi was called to a farmhouse, where she was kept back on the pretext of a party. There, she was murdered by slitting her throat with a knife. After that, her body was packed in a sack and thrown into the canal embankment. Mobile location data from nearby areas helped police reach the suspects. According to the postmortem report, the accused first slit Rakhi’s throat, then stabbed her multiple times in the chest and back. On Friday, Rakhi’s younger brother Vikas reached Saharanpur. He refused to take the body back to Baghpat. After police counselled him, Vikas performed Rakhi’s last rites in Saharanpur itself, in the presence of police.

stories.title: BJP still strong in UP but needs candidate overhaul:Voters upset with MLAs; SP may gain more seats
stories.summary: With barely eight months left for the enforcement of the model code of conduct ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, political parties have ramped up preparations. A large-scale ground survey indicates that while the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) remains the preferred choice among voters in the state, it faces a significant challenge—public dissatisfaction with many of its sitting MLAs and ministers. SP appears to gaining ground The findings suggest that for the BJP to retain power in the 2027 Assembly elections, it may need to replace several incumbent legislators. At the same time, the Samajwadi Party (SP) appears to be gaining ground, with its projected seat tally rising. Meanwhile, BJP’s allies are witnessing erosion in their support base, a shift that may ultimately benefit the BJP itself. Widespread public discontent against MLAs The survey highlights deep public resentment toward elected representatives across party lines. Out of BJP’s 257 MLAs, voters expressed dissatisfaction with 222. The primary reasons cited were lack of development work, poor accessibility, and unsatisfactory behavior. Senior journalist Harshvardhan Tripathi noted that many MLAs have failed to connect with the public. According to him, representatives who remained distant—often not stepping out of their comfort zones to engage with constituents—naturally invited criticism. He added that over the past four years, even the opposition has failed to mount significant public-interest movements, leaving citizens to struggle with routine issues at local administrative levels such as tehsils, police stations, and block offices. The trend is not limited to the ruling party. Among SP’s 105 MLAs, 91 also faced public dissatisfaction, indicating a broader systemic issue in political representation. Replacing candidates has historically benefited BJP The survey underscores a crucial electoral pattern: changing candidates has previously worked in BJP’s favor. In the 2022 Assembly elections, BJP and its ally Apna Dal (S) dropped 104 out of their 318 sitting MLAs—approximately 32%—due to anti-incumbency sentiments. Of the new candidates fielded, 80 went on to win, validating the strategy. In contrast, during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, BJP largely retained its sitting MPs despite local-level dissatisfaction. The result was a sharp decline in seats—from 62 to 33 in Uttar Pradesh—highlighting the risks of ignoring voter sentiment. Hindutva and Development still drive BJP’s popularity Despite dissatisfaction with individual representatives, the BJP continues to enjoy strong support as a party. The survey found that even though around 88% of MLAs from both ruling and opposition parties faced criticism, voters still preferred the BJP overall. Senior journalist Sunita Aron explained that elections have increasingly become leader-centric. In Uttar Pradesh, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath remains a dominant figure for the BJP, while Akhilesh Yadav leads the SP. As voters focus more on leadership and party identity rather than individual candidates, legislators have become less accountable for development work. She added that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s image—centered on Hindutva and development—continues to resonate with voters, keeping the BJP ahead despite local grievances. SP gains seats but faces challenges in Western UP The survey suggests that the Samajwadi Party is improving its position, with its seat count projected to rise from 105 to around 135. The gains are primarily seen in regions such as Purvanchal, Awadh, Braj, and Kanpur-Bundelkhand. However, SP faces setbacks in western Uttar Pradesh, where it needs to recalibrate its social and political equations. The region has a complex demographic mix, including Jats, Muslims, Gurjars, and Dalits. Apart from Muslims, SP lacks a strong independent vote base here. Previously, SP benefited from its alliance with the Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD), which has since ended. The party is now attempting to rebuild its support among Jats and Gurjars. Sunita Aron pointed out that polarization remains a significant factor in western UP, particularly in Muslim-majority districts. Additionally, parties led by Asaduddin Owaisi and Chandrashekhar Azad are also influencing voter dynamics in the region. BJP’s recent developmental push in western UP has further strengthened its position. Allies losing ground, BJP gains indirect advantage Another key takeaway from the survey is the declining influence of BJP’s allies, including Apna Dal (S), Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP), Nishad Party, and RLD. These parties, often centered around caste-based politics, appear to be losing their support base. Out of 33 MLAs from these allied parties, only three received positive feedback from voters, while 30 faced dissatisfaction. However, these allies remained the top choice in only eight constituencies. This decline could indirectly benefit the BJP. In regions like Purvanchal, where allies like Nishad Party, SBSP, and Apna Dal (S) have traditionally held sway, their weakening support base appears to be shifting toward the BJP. Sunita Aron observed that voters are increasingly consolidating around national or major regional parties, moving away from smaller caste-based outfits. Harshvardhan Tripathi added that allies often engage in pressure politics while being part of the government, which can undermine their credibility among voters. Ministers face greater scrutiny and Higher expectations The survey also highlights dissatisfaction with ministers, which is even more pronounced than with MLAs. When an MLA becomes a minister, public expectations from that constituency rise significantly, with hopes of accelerated development. Tripathi explained that the BJP has been in power in Uttar Pradesh for nearly nine years, and several leaders have held ministerial positions for extended periods. Over time, expectations from both the public and party workers increase. While broader themes like Hindutva and development may resonate at the macro level, neglect of local issues and poor responsiveness to party workers’ concerns can fuel resentment. If ministers are perceived as unapproachable or indifferent, dissatisfaction intensifies further. He warned that a lack of coordination between the government, party organization, and grassroots workers could create challenges for the BJP in the upcoming elections if not addressed in time. Caste remains a factor, but not the only one Interestingly, the survey found that voters did not explicitly cite caste as a primary factor in their preferences. Among various reasons for liking or disliking candidates, caste was the least mentioned. This suggests a shift in voter behaviour. While caste dynamics continue to influence politics in Uttar Pradesh, voters appear to be increasingly considering factors such as performance, accessibility, and leadership. If caste alone were decisive, BJP’s allies—many of whom rely heavily on caste-based support—would not be witnessing a decline. The findings indicate that no party can rely solely on caste equations to secure an electoral victory in the state.

stories.title: 7 trapped as water tank collapses in Bareilly:Victims were playing cards underneath; structure was built 4 years ago under Jal Jeevan Mission
stories.summary: In Bareilly on Monday, 7 people were trapped after a water tank of the Jal Jeevan Mission collapsed. All of them were sitting near the tank playing cards. As soon as the tank fell, there was a very loud explosion-like sound. Hearing this, the villagers rushed to the spot. When they saw, the entire tank had collapsed. The villagers immediately removed the debris and pulled out the trapped people. They were immediately rushed to the hospital for treatment. One of the injured is said to be in serious condition. Upon receiving information about the accident, police administration and SDRF teams reached the spot. They started removing the debris. The incident occurred in the Bhamora area at 5 PM. See 2 pictures of the rescue Tank was built at a cost of over 3 crore Jal Nigam had built a tank four years ago in Sardar Nagar Gram Panchayat of Bhamora development block, Alampur Jafrabad. On Monday evening around 5 PM, the tank suddenly collapsed. As a result, 7 people playing cards near the tank were buried under the debris. Upon receiving the information, officials reached the spot, and the police sent all the injured to the hospital. The injured include Dori Lal, Veerpal, Arjun, Ravindra alias Dabbu, and Bedpal. Villagers Avnesh Kumar, Naresh Sharma, Sanjeev Pathak, Sachin Chauhan, and others stated that the government had constructed the water tank in 2022 under the Jal Jeevan Mission at a cost of three crore sixty-two lakh eighty-seven thousand rupees. Water had reached homes 8 months ago Pradhan's husband Sartaj Mansoori said that contractor Amrish had carried out the construction under the supervision of Jal Nigam's JE Nityanand. After the construction of the tank, water supply through taps to every household had started for the villagers eight months ago. Upon receiving the information, CO Nitin Kumar, who arrived with the police, sent all the injured to private and government hospitals. SDM Aonla Bidushi Singh reached the spot along with ADM E. The administration team is removing the debris of the tank.

stories.title: UP staff transfers scheduled between 5 and 31 May:New policy gets approval, summons will come via WhatsApp
stories.summary: Transfers of 1.6 million employees and officers in UP will be done from May 5 to May 31. The Yogi cabinet approved the transfer policy for 2026-27 on Monday. Officers and employees who have completed three years of service in a district and seven years in a division will be subject to transfer. Couples in government service will be posted at the same location. Relief will be provided to disabled employees and those suffering from serious illnesses. 29 proposals have been approved in the cabinet. Parliamentary Affairs and Finance Minister Suresh Khanna stated at the Lok Bhawan Media Center that 20 percent of employees and officers will be transferred compared to the total sanctioned posts in departments. Know the important decisions Now e-summons will be issued To expedite the disposal of pending cases in the state's courts, the state government has now implemented the e-summons system. Cases used to take time for disposal due to summons issued by the court not being served on time, or due to the concerned complainant, plaintiff, or witness not accepting personal summons. In the cabinet meeting, the Uttar Pradesh E-Evidence Management Rules, Uttar Pradesh Electronic Summons Issuance and Service Rules 2026, and Community Service Guidelines 2026 have been approved. Under this, summons can now be issued via email and WhatsApp, and these will be considered authorized. Farmers will get compensation for towers and power lines Energy Minister Arvind Kumar Sharma said that in the state, 765, 490, 220, and 132 KV high-tension lines are laid through farmers' fields. Large electricity towers are also installed. Before 2018, there was no provision for compensation for power lines and towers passing through fields. However, this provision was made in 2018, but farmers were not satisfied due to the very low compensation amount in that provision. Because of this, there were difficulties in laying power lines and installing towers in the fields. The government has now made a provision to increase the compensation amount. For the land located within a one-meter radius of the spot where an electricity tower will be installed in the field, the farmer will be given double the compensation based on the circle rate. For laying electricity lines across the field, up to 30 percent of the land's value will be given as compensation. Solar Plant to be Installed in Jalaun The Energy Minister stated that the use of renewable energy is increasing in the state. To reduce global warming and promote green energy, a 500 MW capacity solar plant will be installed in Jalaun. For its installation, in this plant being set up under the joint auspices of Uttar Pradesh State Electricity Generation Corporation and Coal India Limited, 45 percent share will belong to the state government and 56 percent to Coal India Limited. Power Stations to be established in YEIDA The Energy Minister stated that new industries are being established in the Yamuna Expressway Authority area in Noida. To improve the electricity supply system there, three new 400/220 KVA power stations will be built. It will cost 653 crore rupees. Industries coming up in the Greater Noida and Yamuna Authority areas will benefit from this. One District One Dish Scheme Approved MSME Minister Rakesh Sachan informed that the Cabinet has approved the One District-One Dish scheme. The scheme will give national and international recognition to one dish from each district. A unique dish from the district will be selected for the scheme. Efforts will be made to improve their packaging and quality. Along with developing a logo for the dish, it will be branded. By training relevant traders and artisans, the dishes will be made available in various festivals and events. Along with increasing their production, a market will also be provided. He said, UP holds a distinct identity in traditional cuisine. Agra's Petha, Mathura's Peda, Gorakhpur's Litti Chokha, Meerut's Gajak, Jaunpur's Imarti, Farrukhabad's Dalmoth - all these dishes have been the identity of these districts for centuries. Efforts will be made to increase income by giving them a distinct identity at national and international levels. He informed that a division-wise list has been prepared. To effectively implement the scheme, a vendor conference will be organized at Rashtra Prerna Sthal in Lucknow. A conference of food vendors and confectioners will be held, and universities and technical institutions working in the food sector will be included in this conference. Information on technology and packaging in the food sector will be provided, and excellent dishes will be showcased by setting up stalls. Under the scheme, investors will be given up to 25 percent subsidy. Textile parks will be established Rakesh Sachan informed that the state government had set a target to establish 10 textile parks in the state under the Sant Kabir Textile and Apparel Park scheme. Currently, the work of establishing a textile park is underway in Varanasi, and 75 acres of land have been acquired. In the cabinet meeting held on Monday, textile parks will be established on the land of spinning mills: 79 acres in Amroha, 79 acres in Baheri of Bareilly, 40 acres in Sant Kabir Nagar, and 52 acres in Nagina of Bijnor. Investors have been invited through master developers, and these parks will provide employment to millions of people, creating jobs in the textile sector in UP. A private university will be established in Firozabad Higher Education Minister Yogendra Upadhyay said, the Cabinet has approved issuing a letter of intent to Amardeep Memorial Trust for the establishment of Amardeep University Firozabad, under the Uttar Pradesh Private Universities Act. The proposal to grant a letter of authority for the operation of Metro University in Noida has also been approved. 35 crore saplings will be planted Minister of State for Forest and Environment, Arun Saxena, informed that 35 crore saplings will be planted in the financial year 2026-27 to increase green cover and tree plantation. A demand of Rs 147 crore has been made for tree plantation in departments, undertakings, railways, defense, industrial units, private and government institutions of the state government and the Government of India. Saplings will be planted with public participation. 30 percent fruit-bearing trees will be planted. 150 CM Fellows to be recruited Alok Kumar, Principal Secretary of the Industrial Development Department, informed that an OTD cell was constituted under the chairmanship of the District Magistrate to make the state's economy a one trillion dollar economy. To assist this cell, two OTD CM Fellows will be deployed in each district. One should be proficient in the field of economic development and the other OTD Fellow will provide services related to data analysis. The age limit for CM Fellows has been set at 40 years, while a monthly honorarium of 50 thousand rupees will be given. A housing allowance of ten thousand rupees will be provided. A laptop worth 40 thousand rupees will be given. CM Fellows will be recruited for three years, after which their tenure can be extended by one year at a time. CM Fellows who have served for three years will get age relaxation in recruitment examinations conducted by various recruitment commissions of the state government. Finance Minister Suresh Khanna informed that for the smooth and efficient functioning of the judicial work of the High Court Lucknow Bench, the tenure of 145 Law Clerks will be extended from two years to three years. A monthly honorarium of 40 thousand rupees is given. Finance Minister Suresh Khanna said that just as Tata has taken 150 ITIs, similarly, to impart technical knowledge to children, Dream Skill Labs will be established in 150 government schools in collaboration with Nelco Network Products Ltd. In the first phase, labs will be established at every divisional headquarters in the state. 68 percent of the money will be from Tata Nelco, and 32 percent will be from the state government. On this, Tata Nelco will spend 1360 crore rupees and the department will spend 640.20 crore rupees. In the first phase, one Dream Skill Lab will be established at each divisional headquarters.

stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Lotus blooms in West Bengal; Vijay’s TVK storm sweeps Tamil Nadu Vote counting is underway across 293 seats in West Bengal, with polling in one seat scheduled for 21 May. 2. 8 die after car ploughs into crowd in Ambedkar Nagar An out-of-control car ran over people standing on the road in Ambedkar Nagar, UP. 8 people, including 2 real brothers, died in the accident. It is being reported that around 12 midnight on Sunday, two bikes first collided, in which both bike riders were seriously injured. 3. 38 IAS transferred in UP, Firozabad DM removed over iPhone allegations The Yogi government late Sunday night transferred 38 IAS officers. District Magistrates (DMs) of eight districts have been changed. Rinku Singh Rahi, who had submitted a conditional resignation and later withdrew it, has been given a posting after nine months. 4. Gaurav Gogoi loses from Assam's Jorhat Counting of votes is underway for the Assam, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Puducherry assembly constituencies. 5. Man who killed mother, 4 children shot dead in Ambedkar Nagar encounter The police shot down the accused who murdered a mother and 4 children in an encounter in Ambedkar Nagar, UP. The encounter between accused Aamir (19) and the police took place on Monday morning at 5 AM near Newtariya Bypass. 6. Prayagraj woman seen sleeping on notes claims to be victim of ‘love jihad’ Pallavi Singh, 32, has been in the spotlight after climbing a water tank in Prayagraj and threatening suicide. She is known on social media for making reels, including videos showing ₹500 notes spread across her bed, and is also said to have an interest in weapons. 7. Indian stock markets zoom as BJP clinches Assam, West Bengal Indian share markets opened higher on Monday, 4 April 2026, amid cooling oil prices after US President Donald Trump promised safe passage of non-Iranian ships through the Strait of Hormuz. 8. Kashi MLA presents jhalmuri instead of bouquet: City BJP celebrates Bengal victory Vote counting is underway for 293 seats in West Bengal. In the initial trends, the BJP has gained a majority. Seeing this, BJP workers in UP have started celebrating. In Varanasi, Agra, and Jhansi, BJP workers burst firecrackers and danced enthusiastically. 9. Tavera hits truck at 100 kmph, 6 dead in Jalaun; group was returning from Ayodhya In Jalaun, a Tavera car, travelling at 100 kmph, crashed into the back of a truck on the highway. 6 devotees died in the accident, while 4 are seriously injured. The Tavera occupants were going to Lalitpur after visiting Ramlala in Ayodhya. The accident was so horrific that the car was badly damaged and its occupants were trapped. 10. Mahavir Phogat supports Vinesh, claims 'WFI should be dissolved' After Olympian wrestler Vinesh Phogat accused former president of the Wrestling Federation of India, Brijbhushan Singh, of sexual harassment, Olympic coach Mahavir Phogat has come out in her support.

stories.title: Yogi’s Bengal campaign sees BJP leading in 31 seats:CM achieves 89% strike rate, Rajnath at 83% and Keshav at 78%
stories.summary: In the West Bengal Assembly elections, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath campaigned on the highest number of seats among leaders from the state, covering 35 constituencies. According to Election Commission data on results and trends available till 8 pm, BJP candidates have either won or are leading on 31 of these seats, which is about 89%. The Chief Minister also campaigned on two seats in Assam. On these, one has been won by the BJP and the other by its ally Asom Gana Parishad. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh campaigned on six seats, of which BJP candidates are leading or have won on five seats, around 83%. Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya’s campaign seats have also shown strong performance, with BJP candidates leading on about 78% of them. CM Yogi cornered TMC on 5 issues 1. Harassment of BJP workers CM Yogi launched a sharp attack on the plight of Bengal, saying that there was widespread chaos under Trinamool rule. The homes of BJP workers like Swarup Ghosh, Palash Ghosh, and Utpal Das were destroyed. He targeted the vote-bank traders who are changing Bengal's demography and questioned Mamata Didi's silence on the killing of Dalit Hindus in Bangladesh. 2. Cut money with the help of sand, land, and cattle mafia CM Yogi raised the issue of sand, coal, land, and cattle mafia in the Trinamool Congress government. He said that they are sucking Bengal dry. In 15 years, TMC has turned Bengal into a hub of terror, mafia rule, cut money, and corruption. 3. West Bengal's Demography is Changing CM Yogi kept asking the public in all his rallies that Bengal's identity is not from the Kaaba, but from Maa Kalibari. Then, taking a dig at Mamata Banerjee and her nephew Abhishek Banerjee, he said that the aunt-nephew duo wants to erase Bengal's existence. 4. UP Model vs. Bengal's Plight CM Yogi reiterated in every rally that before 2017, the condition of UP was similar to that of Bengal. He would say in his speech, "Earlier, riots used to happen during festivals in UP, curfews were imposed. When the double engine government was formed in 2017, everything changed. Now no curfew, no riots. Bulldozers sent goons and mafias to hell. UP has now become the growth engine of the country's economy." 5. Mention of Bengal's glorious history In rallies, the CM would remind people of Bengal's golden past, saying that Bengal gave spirituality, culture, art, and education to the country. At one time, Bengal was the backbone of India's GDP. Congress, the Left, and then TMC made it poor. Referring to the 1905 partition of Bengal protest and the Swadeshi movement, he appealed to Bengalis to unite again. He also mentioned settling 331 Hindu families from Bangladesh in Lakhimpur Kheri. Results of seats where Yogi held rallies and roadshows How CM Yogi's visit is decided According to people associated with the BJP state organization, the CM's visit is decided based on the guidelines of the National Election Management Committee. For this, the BJP's state unit and the party headquarters in Delhi play a key role. The demand for Yogi's visit is first made by the BJP's state units. The states send their demand to the Delhi party headquarters. From here, the visits are finalized. Along with this, the Election Management Committee also decides the visits of star campaigners after considering the seat situation, equations, and issues in the states. This information must be given to the state unit and the CM three to four days in advance. Sometimes, visits are also fixed suddenly. BJP in North 24 Parganas, under the charge of Suresh Rana Former UP Cabinet Minister Suresh Rana was made in-charge of North 24 Parganas. Out of 33 assembly constituencies here, BJP candidates are leading in 14, while TMC candidates are leading in 17. Additionally, several current and former UP MLAs were assigned responsibility for 47 assembly constituencies. Out of these, BJP is leading in 30. Among these prominent leaders are Dayashankar Mishra Dayalu, Minister of State Dinesh Khatik, Sanjay Gangwar, former MP Ajay Mishra Teni, Subrat Pathak, Swati Singh, Upendra Tiwari, Anand Shukla, MLC Dharmendra Bhardwaj, and Arun Pathak. BJP leads in 2 seats campaigned by Ravi Kishan BJP leading on 30 seats in Medinipur, under JPS Rathore's charge JPS Rathore, Cooperation Minister in the UP government, was given charge of Medinipur in West Bengal. BJP candidates are leading on 30 out of 35 seats here. He has also been in charge of the West Bengal Assembly election management branch in 2021. He has handled similar responsibilities in the UP elections of 2017 and 2022. BJP leading on 2 seats campaigned by Brajesh Pathak Yogi campaigned in 31 seats in Bihar, BJP won 27 Six months ago, in the Bihar elections, UP CM Yogi Adityanath held 31 public meetings and rallies. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav campaigned in 22 seats in Bihar in favor of the Grand Alliance without contesting any seat. The UP CM had a significant impact on the results. His win strike rate was over 87 percent. 27 out of 31 NDA candidates registered a win. Whereas Akhilesh Yadav's strike rate was merely 9 percent. The Grand Alliance won only two seats where he campaigned.

stories.title: Maulana’s death on Bareilly train sparks lynching claims:Wife alleges assault over identity, seeks probe; police register case begin investigation
stories.summary: The death of Maulana Tausif Raza Mazhari, who travelled from Bihar to attend the Urs in Bareilly, has taken a serious turn. His wife Tabassum has alleged that he was attacked on a train and thrown off, calling it a case of mob lynching. She questioned Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, asking whether people with beards and caps can live safely in Uttar Pradesh. Wife recounts final phone call Tabassum said her husband called her from the train on April 26, saying some people were beating him. During a video call, she saw men pulling his collar and slapping him while accusing him of theft. He kept insisting he was a madrasa teacher carrying only books and clothes. Claims made by the family Body found, police cite fall theory The next morning, Bareilly GRP informed Tabassum that her husband’s body was found on railway tracks. Police initially suggested he may have fallen from the train due to heat or drowsiness, a claim the family has strongly rejected. Complaint filed, probe underway Tabassum reached Bareilly from Kishanganj and filed a complaint seeking a murder case. GRP Inspector Sushil Kumar Verma confirmed that a case has been registered against unknown persons. SP City Manush Parik said action will follow based on investigation findings. Reactions and demand for justice Political and religious voices have raised concerns. AIMIM leader Nadeem Qureshi alleged that people with a specific identity are being targeted. Mufti Tausif Nurani of Dargah Ala Hazrat called the incident a conspiracy and demanded an impartial probe. What the family is demanding Tabassum said their marriage was less than two years old and her husband was the sole earner. She has vowed to continue her fight until justice is delivered.

stories.title: Repeated calls to Sambhal DM raise alarm:Man asked about jail 17 times; later claims police arrested him
stories.summary: In Sambhal, a young man called the District Magistrate 17 times. He later said he had done it just for fun. During the calls, he even asked the DM whether he would be punished. The officer had said no, but the youth now claims he is being sent to jail despite only asking about his well-being. Police have charged the man with disturbing public peace. The City Magistrate has sent him to 14 days of judicial custody. A day earlier, he had recited poetry and praised MP Ziaur Rahman Barq at a public event. The incident took place in the Hayatnagar police station area. Now read the full story Police have arrested Arafat, son of Ejaz, a resident of Mohalla Nawabkhel Kacha Bazar in Saraitareen. On May 2, Arafat called the DM's CUG number 17 times and harassed him by talking about various things. The young man sometimes asked the DM about his well-being and sometimes asked if he would take action against him. Several times the call was received from the control room. After this, the police arrested the young man on Sunday evening. Late on Sunday night, the DM was transferred to Moradabad. Arafat said that he had called the DM only to ask, "DM sir, are you well?" "I didn't know that asking about well-being would result in such a big punishment." According to Arafat, he made this call for fun. Arafat said that he had asked the DM if there would be any punishment, to which the DM sir had said 'no', and now look, the police are taking me away, sending me to jail. Poetry was recited at the SP MP's event On May 2, an event was organised in the Nakhasa police station area of Sambhal, whose chief guest was SP MP from Sambhal, Ziaur Rahman Barq. Many people were present on the stage with the MP at that event. Arafat recited poetry saying, May this light of life remain safe, the world can understand me when MP Ziaur Rahman Barq understands me. Did not bow down out of fear of the city, the lamp was not extinguished by the winds Who says the Taj Mahal is beautiful? It's just a stone idol; Shafiqur Rahman's face is even more beautiful than the Taj Mahal. What are you writing, Aamir? What are you writing, Aamir, I did not bow down out of fear of the city, my lamp was not extinguished by the winds, it is the grace of my mother's prayers, darkness did not befall my fate." The MP clapped in praise of Arafat, and then the young man left. Sent to jail after a medical examination After the arrest, the police conducted Arafat's medical examination at the District Combined Hospital. After this, he was presented in the City Magistrate's Court. Magistrate Sudhir Kumar, taking cognisance of the police report of breach of peace, sent Arafat to jail for 14 days. City Magistrate Sudhir Kumar said that The youth was presented in court by Hayatnagar police station. He was repeatedly calling and harassing the DM, and was (fined/charged) for disturbing the peace. As he did not furnish bail, he has been sent to jail. If the youth's bail is presented in court, further action will be taken after considering it.

stories.title: 'Please save me', shouts blood-soaked man:Tavera hits truck at 100 kmph, killing 6; group was returning from Ayodhya trip
stories.summary: In Jalaun, a Tavera car, travelling at 100 kmph, crashed into the back of a truck on the highway. 6 devotees died in the accident, while 4 are seriously injured. The Tavera occupants were going to Lalitpur after visiting Ramlala in Ayodhya. The accident was so horrific that the car was badly damaged and its occupants were trapped. They writhed in pain in the car for 30 minutes. A video of this has surfaced. In it, three youths are stuck between the seat and the dashboard. Two died shortly after. While the third youth kept screaming - Brother, sir, save me.... Upon receiving information about the accident, the police arrived and cut open the car's door with a gas cutter to rescue the injured. The accident occurred in Kalpi, 55 km from the city, on the Jhansi-Kanpur Highway. The police's initial investigation revealed that the accident happened because the driver dozed off. The devotees had not worn seat belts, due to which the airbags also did not deploy. This is why 6 people lost their lives in the accident. See 3 pictures of the accident- Patients writhed in the ambulance for 10 minutes Shashikant Tiwari (49), a resident of Mehroni, Lalitpur, had gone to Ayodhya for darshan with his family and relatives. There were 10 people in the car. They were returning by car after darshan early Monday morning. As soon as their car reached Jholhupur turn in Kalpi area at 6 am, the driver dozed off, causing the Tavera to lose control and collide with a truck moving in front. After the accident, there was chaos at the spot. Local people rushed to the scene. They saw that people were badly trapped in the car. Attempts were made to rescue them, but they were unsuccessful. After this, the police were informed. The police called for a gas cutter. After this, the car doors were cut and everyone was pulled out. By then, 4 people had already died. Police rescued 6 people and sent the injured to the medical college by ambulance. But there was no ward boy present. The patients suffered in the ambulance for about 10 minutes. After this, the people present there somehow pulled out the injured and took them to the emergency ward. Here, two more people died. The remaining 4 were referred to a higher center in Kanpur after primary treatment. DM Rajesh Kumar Pandey said- Devotees from Mehroni had come to participate in the idol consecration ceremony held at the Ram-Janaki temple on April 30. During this, some idols were damaged, which were to be immersed with proper rituals. In this regard, 10 devotees came to Ayodhya on the evening of May 2. They immersed the idols in the Saryu river. They offered prayers at Ram Mandir and Hanumangarhi. They were returning to Lalitpur on the morning of May 4, when the accident occurred. Those who died in the accident have been identified as Shashikant Tripathi, Krishnakant Nayak, Deepak Tiwari, Swami Prasad Tiwari, Manoj Bhondle, and Deshraj Namdev. The injured include Harimohan, Anshul, Shivanand, and Bhushan Tiwari.

stories.title: Kashi MLA presents jhalmuri instead of bouquet:City BJP celebrates, chants 'Har-Har Modi, Ghar-Ghar Modi'
stories.summary: Vote counting is underway for 293 seats in West Bengal. In the initial trends, the BJP has gained a majority. Seeing this, BJP workers in UP have started celebrating. In Varanasi, Agra, and Jhansi, BJP workers burst firecrackers and danced enthusiastically. In Kashi, BJP workers chanted slogans like "Har-Har Modi, Ghar-Ghar Modi" and "Mamata Banerjee Murdabad" (Down with Mamata Banerjee). On the Ganga ghats, people from the boatman community applied gulal to each other. A BJP woman worker associated with the Bengali community blew a conch shell. They also performed Ganga Aarti. BJP worker Reena said - "During Mamata Didi's rule in Bengal, there has been a lot of oppression." MLA Saurabh Srivastava from Varanasi gave Jhalmuri instead of a bouquet to Sunil Bansal, the in-charge of the Bengal elections. Actually, PM Modi had eaten Jhalmuri during the election campaign. Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya attacked Akhilesh Yadav. He wrote on X: The public is now unwilling to listen to SP chief Akhilesh Yadav. His 'Bhaiya' M. K. Stalin from Tamil Nadu and 'Didi' Mamata Banerjee from Bengal have also been pushed to the sidelines by the public. Now Akhilesh Yadav should abandon 'dreams of power' in Uttar Pradesh in 2027. stories.title: 3 cops, including Sub-Inspector, line-attached over assault:Woman advocate had made allegations of molestation and assault
stories.summary: DCP City Syed Ali Abbas has taken action against three police personnel, including the Station House Officer (SHO) of Lohamandi police station in Agra, over allegations of molestation and assault of a woman advocate who had come to represent a victim. In a report submitted to the court, he found the personnel guilty of indiscipline and has ordered their line-attached. According to the complaint, a woman advocate from the Mantola police station area visited the Lohamandi police station on March 11, along with a victim, to file a case related to assault. She alleged that SHO Anuj Mishra, Head Constable Usman, and Constable Munendra tried to complicate the matter during the process. When they protested, they were misbehaved with. When her sister started recording a video, the police snatched her mobile phone and twisted her arm. They were assaulted, and both sisters were inappropriately touched. They were made to sit at the police station until midnight. The next day, they staged a protest at the police station gate and filed a complaint with Police Commissioner Deepak Kumar. When no action was taken, they approached the court. The court sought a report from DCP City Syed Ali Abbas. In his report, he stated that the woman advocate had come with the complainant and spoke loudly in anger and started recording a video. CCTV footage did not show any instance of physical contact, snatching of the mobile phone, or molestation. However, it was found that inappropriate remarks were made to the advocate in the presence of the Station House Officer. The advocate’s presence with the complainant was not recorded in the general diary. The DGP’s instructions to promptly hear and address the concerns of women visitors were also not followed. As a result, all three personnel were line-attached.

stories.title: Love-hate bond between two women turns deadly:One lady kills another’s son to get revenge; husbands had left them over close friendship
stories.summary: A 42-year-old woman in Saharanpur allegedly killed the 14-year-old son of her 35-year-old friend, raising questions about what led to the crime. According to police sources, the two women were childhood friends and shared a very close bond. They had even left their respective husbands and were living together for some time. However, tensions began to grow as their children got older. A financial dispute of around ₹6 lakh further strained their relationship. What started as a long-standing friendship eventually turned into bitterness, culminating in the killing of the boy. Police are investigating how a bond that began in childhood deteriorated to this extent. Read the full story Childhood spent together, friendship later turned into a deep relationship Police said that Pooja and Jyoti had known each other since childhood. Their friendship kept growing deeper. In childhood, both played together, studied, and shared every joy and sorrow. Gradually, the friendship became even deeper. Later, both developed intimate relations as well. But, in the meantime, the family got Pooja and Jyoti married. Jyoti was married to Bal Krishna Bharti, who lived in the Numaish Camp area. She had 4 sons, Anurag, Vishal, Vikas, and Anshuman. The eldest son, Anurag, is about 25 years old, while the youngest son, Anshuman, is 14 years old. Meanwhile, Pooja was married to Ravi Mohan. She also had a daughter. Did not leave each other's company even after marriage On the other hand, even after Jyoti and Pooja got married, their closeness to each other did not diminish. Both continued to meet each other. They used to visit each other's homes. They used to roam around together. Everything was going normally. But, about 10 years ago (in 2016), Pooja's husband caught both of them in a compromising position. After this, there was a huge fight between both families. Despite this, Jyoti and Pooja were not ready to separate from each other. After this, the matter escalated to the point that both were abandoned by their husbands. Then both started living in houses about 500 meters away from each other. As the children grew up, the conflict increased Gradually, Pooja and Jyoti's children also grew up. Meanwhile, Pooja got her daughter married. However, the children came to know about their mothers' relationship. The children started opposing this relationship. This increased the tension in both households. The matter escalated to the point where fights started breaking out between Jyoti's elder son, Anurag, and Pooja. Despite this, Pooja had transferred one of her shops to Jyoti's elder son, Anurag, about a year and a half ago. She started demanding ₹6 lakh in exchange for the shop. However, Anurag was not ready to pay the money. Meanwhile, about 9 months ago, a major fight broke out between Anurag and Pooja. The matter escalated so much that both women decided to end their mutual relationship. However, Pooja remained adamant about getting her money. When defamed, she decided to take revenge On the other hand, instead of paying Pooja ₹6 lakh, Anurag started spreading false rumors about her. This made Pooja angry, and she decided to take revenge. She started plotting various schemes. Meanwhile, on May 1st, Pooja was going somewhere on her scooter. She saw Jyoti's youngest son, Anshuman, on the way. When Pooja asked Anshuman to sit on the scooter, he agreed. After this, Pooja took him to the big canal outside the city. While talking, she took him right to the edge of the canal and pushed him, causing him to fall into the canal. After this, Pooja returned home on her scooter. She did not mention this entire incident to anyone. Meanwhile, when Anshuman did not return home for a long time, Jyoti started worrying about him. Jyoti and her children started searching for Anshuman, but he was nowhere to be found. After this, Jyoti filed a missing person report for her son. To search for the child, the police checked the CCTVs around his house. In the CCTV, a woman was seen taking Anshuman away on a scooter. When the same footage was shown to Jyoti, she identified the woman as Pooja. After this, the police arrested Pooja at her house. Child's body found floating in canal after 2 days At first, Pooja kept misleading the police. But she kept getting trapped in her own answers. After this, she confessed to committing the murder. Pooja told the police that she had pushed Anshuman into the canal. After this, on May 2 (Saturday), a rescue operation was conducted in the main canal based on Pooja's identification. Two divers searched throughout the day, but the child could not be found. Then, on May 3 (Sunday), passersby near the canal saw the child's body floating in the water and informed the police. After this, the police recovered Anshuman's body. Pooja said that I got scared During police interrogation, Pooja said that I had no intention of killing Anshuman. I just took Anshuman out with me for a walk. When Anshuman didn't reach home for a long time, his family members started calling me. They were asking about Anshuman. This scared me. That's why I pushed Anshuman into the canal. His mother and brother also used to fight with me often. I had no enmity with him.

stories.title: Prayagraj woman seen sleeping on notes claims ‘love jihad’:Climbed water tank to prove innocence; husband claims she married four times
stories.summary: Pallavi Singh, 32, has been in the spotlight after climbing a water tank in Prayagraj and threatening suicide. She is known on social media for making reels, including videos showing ₹500 notes spread across her bed, and is also said to have an interest in weapons. While, she is currently drawing attention for her online persona and claims of a lavish lifestyle, she has been linked to controversies in the past. Police records indicate that around 14 cases are registered against her. Her husband, Mohammad Alam, has alleged that Pallavi was previously married multiple times and has had relationships with several men. He has also accused her of living a luxury lifestyle using other people’s money. Meanwhile, Pallavi has been drawing parallels between her situation and “The Kerala Story.” Read the complete controversy related to Pallavi... Pallavi also known as Cheeku-Sweety, has 3 Aadhaar cards Pallavi Singh is originally a resident of Ballia. She currently lives in Phaphamau, Prayagraj. On the afternoon of May 2, she climbed onto a 50-foot-high water tank built near Basna Nala in Phaphamau. After a drama that lasted about 9 hours, she could be brought down. Now, Pallavi and her husband are making allegations against each other. Pallavi also has a hobby of making reels with weapons. Her husband Mohammad Alam, who describes himself as a lawyer by profession, says that Pallavi has many names, like Cheeku and Sweety. Pallavi has posted her pictures with many boys on social media. She had also made Aadhaar cards with three different names. Pallavi has married 4 times Pallavi and Mohammad Alam got married in December 2021. Mohammad Alam claims that Pallavi has married several times. In 2018, Pallavi had her first marriage with Dev Anand, a resident of Bihar. She stayed in Bihar for a few months and then returned to Ballia. After that, in 2019, she married Veeru Yadav, a resident of Dhoomnaganj in Prayagraj. She stayed with him for about 4 months. After that, she went away with Deepak Pal, a resident of Naini in Prayagraj. Husband Mohammad Alam claims that he has seen Pallavi with other boys several times. According to the husband, he himself has spent lakhs of rupees on her. He also alleged that Pallavi blackmails people and extorts money from them. More than 14 cases registered It is being reported that more than 14 cases have been registered against Pallavi. Earlier, during a dispute with her husband, there was also an incident of firing at him. Later, there was a settlement between the two, and they started living together again. The husband also said that two days ago, the police from the Cantt area of Lucknow had arrested her and brought her, but she got bail in just one day. After this, with the intention of occupying the house, she climbed on the tank and took this step, and an FIR was registered against her. Pallavi accusing husband of love jihad Meanwhile, Pallavi is now sharing stories on her social media, linking her story to the film 'Kerala Story'. She is making allegations against her own husband. Her husband, Alam, is Muslim. In this situation, she is claiming herself to be a victim of love jihad. Station House Officer Kambodh Singh said- Several cases have already been registered against Pallavi in different police stations. She is also being questioned regarding the picture that surfaced with the notes.

stories.title: Transfer policy for 16 lakh employees to be sealed:Yogi cabinet meeting to approve 14 proposals today
stories.summary: This is big news for 16 lakh employees of UP. In the cabinet meeting to be chaired by CM Yogi on Monday, the transfer policy for 2026-27 for officers and employees will be approved. Employees who have been stationed at the same place for more than three years will be transferred. 20 percent of Group A and B employees and 10 percent of Group C and D employees may be transferred. The transfer process will be completed by the end of May with the approval of departmental ministers. Chief Secretary SP Goyal released the cabinet agenda on Sunday. He informed that the cabinet meeting will be held at the Chief Minister's residence on Monday at 3 PM. About 14 proposals may be approved in the cabinet. 'One District One Dish Scheme' will be approved in the state. Under the scheme, one prominent dish from every district of the state, including Lucknow, Banaras, Kanpur, Gorakhpur, Agra, and Mathura, will be given a new identity. What is special about the new transfer policy? Employees stationed at one place for three years will be transferred The main objective of the new transfer policy is to make the administrative system more transparent and efficient, and to bring new energy by transferring officers and employees who have been stationed at one place for a long time. According to the new policy, employees who have completed three years of service in a district and seven years at the divisional level will be mandatorily transferred. Relief for persons with disabilities Employees with 40 percent or more disability will be able to get an exemption from general transfers. If a disabled employee wants a transfer themselves, they will be given a posting in the district of their choice on a priority basis. Employees who have severely disabled family members, especially mentally challenged or incapacitated children, will also be given posting according to their wishes. Efforts will be made to post husband and wife working in government service in the same district or nearby districts as far as possible, so that family responsibilities can be discharged easily. Group 'A' officers will not be posted in their home district. If the post is at the divisional level, they will not be sent to their home division either. Now know those 14 proposals that will be placed in the meeting Energy Department State Tax Department Food and Logistics Department MSME Department Justice Department Handloom and Textile Industry Agricultural Marketing Department Secondary Education Culture Department Panchayati Department Personnel Department

stories.title: Man who killed mother, 4 children shot dead in encounter:SP said, ‘Accused wanted to marry the woman and usurp her property’
stories.summary: The police shot down the accused who murdered a mother and 4 children in an encounter in Ambedkar Nagar, UP. The encounter between accused Aamir (19) and the police took place on Monday morning at 5 AM near Newtariya Bypass. According to the police, information was received that the accused was planning to escape. Therefore, a cordon was laid to catch him. During this, a suspicious person was seen coming on a bike. When signaled to stop, he turned the bike around and started fleeing. While trying to escape, the bike skidded. Then he started firing at the police. In retaliatory action, the accused was gunned down. He was shot in the chest. During this, a bullet hit the bulletproof jacket of SOG in charge, Vinod Yadav. One inspector and one constable were injured. Actually, on May 2, bodies of four children from the same family were found lying on a bed inside the house in the Muradabad locality, soaked in blood. The children were brutally murdered by being crushed with bricks. Mother Gazia Khatun had gone missing. This had spread terror in the entire area. The police had then suspected that the mother had murdered the children and fled. However, when Gasia's body was found 100 meters away from home on Sunday, the entire police theory was turned upside down. Injury marks were found on Gasia's body. When police started investigating from a murder angle, Aamir's name came up. Police say that the accused was pressuring the woman for marriage. When she refused, he killed her. The case is from the Akbarpur Kotwali area. SP says, ‘Accused wanted to marry the woman and usurp her property’ SP Prachi Singh stated that on May 2, four children were murdered. The mother was missing, after which it was said that the mother committed the murder and fled. The next evening, her dead body was also found in a drain. After this, the investigation of the case was started from a new angle. Nearby CCTVs and DVRs were examined. When the deceased's husband and neighbors were questioned, Aamir's name came up. Aamir had been absconding since the incident. She said that on Monday, early morning, upon receiving information, the police surrounded him and asked him to surrender. He opened fire. He was killed in retaliatory firing. A bike, a pistol, and empty cartridges were recovered from the spot. Property is emerging as the motive for the murder. Gazia's husband had remarried in Saudi Arabia. Therefore, Aamir wanted to marry her and usurp the property. Bodies of 4 children found on May 2, mother reported missing First police named the mother as the murderer, story changed in 24 hours In the initial investigation, police named the mother as the murderer. It was said that after killing the children, the mother jumped from the balcony and fled. SP Prachi Singh said that the police received information that a woman had killed four children and fled. Police immediately reached the spot. I also inspected the scene. A case was registered after taking the complaint, and action was initiated. It appears that the woman who has fled is the one who committed the crime. It could be a property dispute case. Police are investigating all aspects. 24 hours later, when the woman's blood-soaked body was found, the police's previous theory was proven wrong. During inquiries in the neighborhood, neighbors revealed that Aamir, who lived nearby, used to visit Gazia's house. When police investigated Aamir, it came to light that there had been no trace of him since the day of the children's murder. Then, the police started gathering evidence. He was traced. A cordon was set up for his arrest. Early Monday morning, he was cornered near Afzalpur-Akbarpur. He was gunned down in an encounter.

stories.title: Storm causes destruction across UP:Water tank damaged and hanging, wedding mandap blown away; heavy rain in 22 districts, 3 deaths reported
stories.summary: Storms and rain continue across Uttar Pradesh. On Monday morning, hail fell in Ayodhya, Sitapur and Barabanki. Rain was reported in 22 districts, including Lucknow, Varanasi, Gorakhpur and Kanpur. In Lucknow, heavy rain lashed the city for about one and a half hours along with strong winds. The weather changed suddenly at around 8:20 am. Daylight turned dark like night, followed by thunder and intense rainfall. Trees and electricity poles were uprooted due to the storm, causing power cuts in several areas. Drains overflowed in many places. Due to bad weather, an IndiGo flight 6E-6476 travelling from Delhi to Lucknow had to make an emergency landing in Bhopal. Both Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Ministers, Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak, were on board. The aircraft attempted to land three times at Lucknow airport but failed due to strong winds and poor visibility. In Sitapur, Siddharthnagar and Barabanki, wedding tents were blown away. Daytime darkness was also reported in Balrampur. In Kasganj, a house collapsed during the storm, killing two children trapped under the debris. In Sambhal, lightning struck a house, causing part of its roof to collapse. The debris fell on a girl who was sleeping below, leading to her death. The weather department has issued an alert for storms, rain and hail in 64 districts today. Atul Singh, meteorologist of Lucknow, said- In the state, incidents of rain, storms, and lightning will occur for the next few days. Between May 4th and 7th, strong winds will blow at speeds of 40 to 60 km per hour. Hail will fall. Currently, there are no signs of heat waves for a week. Weather pictures- How will the weather be for the next 5 days? Crops damaged by rain, Yogi says, ‘Officers should go to the field’ The spell of rain has been continuing in UP for the last four days. This has caused damage to crops due to rain. Vegetable crops have been particularly affected. Cucumber, melon, and watermelon are expected to suffer major damage. Farmers say that crops may rot due to rain.

stories.title: 38 IAS transfer in UP, 8 DMs changed:Rinku Singh gets posting; Firozabad DM removed over iPhone procurement allegations
stories.summary: The Yogi government late Sunday night transferred 38 IAS officers. District Magistrates (DMs) of eight districts have been changed. Rinku Singh Rahi, who had submitted a conditional resignation and later withdrew it, has been given a posting after nine months. He has been appointed Joint Magistrate in Jalaun. Rajendra Pensiya, who had initiated the search for pilgrimage sites in Sambhal, has been given charge of a bigger district, Moradabad, effectively elevating his stature. Deoria DM Divya Mittal and Firozabad DM Ramesh Ranjan have been removed and sent to the Revenue Department. Divya has been made Special Secretary in the department, while Ramesh Ranjan has been appointed Additional Commissioner (Land Management). In bureaucratic circles, these are considered relatively less significant postings. Divya Mittal had been facing opposition from local public representatives in Deoria, and several complaints against her had reached the government. Meanwhile, Firozabad DM Ramesh Ranjan had been accused by then Tundla Tehsildar Rakhi Sharma of accepting an iPhone as a bribe. Sources say CM Yogi was also unhappy with Ramesh Ranjan’s functioning. Pratapgarh DM Shiv Sahay Awasthi has also been sidelined and appointed CEO of the Rural Road Development Authority. It is said the government was dissatisfied with his work as well. 8 die after car ploughs into crowd in Ambedkar Nagar:Victims gathered to help injured bikers crushed as vehicle loses control at midnight
stories.summary: An out-of-control car ran over people standing on the road in Ambedkar Nagar, UP. 8 people, including 2 real brothers, died in the accident. It is being reported that around 12 midnight on Sunday, two bikes first collided, in which both bike riders were seriously injured. People from nearby reached the spot to help the injured and were trying to take them to the hospital. Meanwhile, an out-of-control Swift Dzire car came and crushed the people. The accident occurred near Ashrafpur Bhuwa Brick Kiln in Jalalpur, 30 km away from the district headquarters. After the accident, local people informed the police. With the help of people, the police took all the injured to CHC Jalalpur. Here, doctors declared 6 people dead. Two injured were referred to the district hospital after first aid. Later, they were sent to Tanda Medical College, where they also died during treatment. The deceased have been identified as Kaifi (32), Uttam Kumar (24), Aditya Kumar (25), Lalchand (24), Raju Gupta (32), and Chhotu, all residents of Ambedkar Nagar. Two victims are yet to be identified.

stories.title: Bike crashes into truck in Bulandshahar:Husband, wife and 3 children die, family was returning from relatives’ house
stories.summary: Five members of a family, including a husband, wife and their three children, were killed after their motorcycle rammed into the rear of a truck in Bulandshahr on Friday evening. The accident took place around 5:30 pm on National Highway-34 in the Dehat Kotwali area. Following the incident, the truck driver fled from the spot with the vehicle. According to police, Uttam Singh (45), a resident of Dhameda Keerat village, had borrowed a motorcycle to visit relatives in Khurja. He had reportedly told the owner that he would return after completing some work. His wife Urmila (40) and their three children, Nishant (8), Disha (6) and Anayra (4), were travelling with him on the same motorcycle. The family was returning home after meeting relatives when the accident occurred. First, see two pictures Motorcycle crashed into truck after it slowed suddenly Police said a truck travelling ahead near Bhaisauli Cut was moving at around 70 kmph when it suddenly slowed down. Uttam Singh’s motorcycle, which was reportedly travelling at high speed behind the truck, lost balance and crashed into the rear of the vehicle. The impact threw the entire family onto the road. Eyewitnesses said the bodies of the husband, wife and children were found piled on top of one another, while the motorcycle lay nearby with its front portion badly damaged. Uttam Singh worked in a private company Uttam Singh was employed at a private company in Secunderabad. He had travelled to Khurja to meet relatives and had borrowed the motorcycle from an acquaintance for the trip. Their eldest son Nishant studied in Class 3, daughter Disha in Class 2, while youngest daughter Anayra was studying in Class 1. The family includes Uttam Singh’s parents, brother, sister-in-law and sister. Police informed the relatives about the accident, though family members had not reached the spot immediately after the incident. SSP and senior officers reached accident site After receiving information, Senior Superintendent of Police Dinesh Kumar Singh, SP City Abhishek Pratap and CO City Prakhar Pandey reached the scene. Police shifted all five victims to hospital, where doctors declared them brought dead. Truck seized, driver absconding Following the crash, the truck driver attempted to flee with the vehicle. Police chased the truck, after which the driver abandoned it and escaped. SSP Dinesh Kumar Singh said the truck bears a Haryana registration number and has been seized by police. He added that all five bodies have been sent for post-mortem examination and efforts are underway to arrest the driver.

stories.title: 2 youths die inside septic tank in Lucknow:One enters first for cleaning, second follows him after seeing no activity
stories.summary: Two labourers died while cleaning a septic tank in Lucknow on Friday afternoon. The incident took place in Navipanah village under the Mal police station area, around 35 km from the district headquarters. According to initial information, labourer Rinku first entered the septic tank for cleaning work. When there was no sound or movement from him for a long time, another labourer, Rajesh, went inside the tank to check on him. However, no response was received from either of them afterwards, triggering panic among people present at the spot. Villagers and police pulled both out unconscious Locals immediately informed the Dial 112 police. With the help of the police team and villagers, both labourers were pulled out of the tank in an unconscious condition. They were rushed to hospital, where doctors declared both of them dead. See 3 pictures- Poisonous gas suspected inside tank Police suspect that poisonous gas inside the septic tank may have caused both labourers to lose consciousness, leading to their deaths. However, officials said the exact cause of death will only be confirmed after the post-mortem report is received. Following the incident, grief spread among the families of the deceased. Inspector Nawab Ahmed of Mal police station said- Two labourers died while cleaning a septic tank. It is suspected that there was some poisonous gas in the tank, due to which both labourers lost their lives.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:Cracks emerge in Taj Mahal’s Royal Gate after storms and heavy rain; Suvendu named new CM of West Bengal
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines- 1. Suvendu Adhikari elected new Chief Minister of West Bengal The BJP legislature party elected Suvendu Adhikari as the next Chief Minister of West Bengal during a meeting in Kolkata. Union Home Minister Amit Shah formally announced his name after the party’s victory. 2. Akhilesh meets Mamata and Stalin, says allies are not abandoned in difficult times SP chief Akhilesh Yadav met Mamata Banerjee in Kolkata and reiterated support to alliance partners after the election results. He later shared photographs with Mamata and Tamil Nadu CM Stalin. 3. Cracks emerge in Taj Mahal’s Royal Gate after storms and heavy rain Visible deterioration has appeared at the Taj Mahal’s historic Royal Gate, with cracks developing and stones shifting from their original positions. The damage reportedly worsened following recent storms and rainfall. 4. TVK set to form government in Tamil Nadu, Vijay likely to be next CM Support from Congress, VCK, CPI and CPI(M) has reportedly strengthened Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam’s numbers after the Assembly election results. Vijay now appears poised to lead the next government in the state. 5. UP government orders conversion of prepaid smart meters into postpaid system The Uttar Pradesh government has directed power departments to convert prepaid electricity meters into postpaid meters. Consumers will also be allowed to clear pending bills till April in ten instalments. 6. Police encounters of child-crime accused raise questions over emerging pattern in UP Within hours of a child rape and murder case in Hardoi, police shot dead the accused in an encounter. The incident marks the third such police killing involving crimes against children in Uttar Pradesh within a month. 7. Iran seizes oil tanker, accuses vessel of disrupting country’s oil exports Iran has seized an oil tanker amid rising tensions with the United States despite claims of a ceasefire remaining in effect. The US military also carried out retaliatory strikes targeting sites linked to attacks on its forces. 8. Prayagraj girl’s skeletal remains found 17 days after alleged murder by boyfriend The skeletal remains of a Class 9 student were recovered from a bushy area in Prayagraj more than two weeks after she allegedly died. Police suspect her 17-year-old boyfriend was involved in the murder. 9. Smart meter backlash may trigger UP cabinet reshuffle, AK Sharma under pressure Public anger over prepaid smart electricity meters has reportedly forced the UP government to reconsider its policy. BJP and RSS leaders are said to have warned the issue could hurt the party electorally. 10. Centre plans major overhaul of 15 lakh government schools from May 2026 The Centre is preparing sweeping reforms aimed at strengthening governance in government schools across India. School Management Committees and parents may get greater control over budgets and expenditure decisions.

stories.title: 'We do not abandon allies in difficult times':Akhilesh meets Mamata and Stalin after election results, shares photos
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav met outgoing chief minister Mamata Banerjee during a courtesy visit to her Kolkata residence on Thursday. Reiterating his continued support to her, Yadav said he or his party never abandon allies during difficult times. “We are not the ones who abandon people in difficult times,” Akhilesh said. The UP leader also shared photographs of his meetings with Mamata and M.K. Stalin in a X post. Akhilesh last met Stalin during an INDIA alliance meeting ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Mamata received Akhilesh at the gate When Akhilesh reached Mamata’s residence, Mamata herself came to the gate to receive him. As Akhilesh moved forward to present her with a shawl, Mamata said, “What was the need for this?” To this, Akhilesh replied, “Didi, you fought, you have not lost.” Om Prakash Rajbhar takes a dig Reacting to the meeting, Uttar Pradesh minister Om Prakash Rajbhar mocked the two leaders. He said Akhilesh had gone to console Mamata by saying, “You have lost only once, while we have lost twice. Let us come together and begin a new series of defeats.” Rajbhar also claimed that when the Bengal election results were being declared, Akhilesh remained silent for four hours and only later decided to meet Mamata. First, see photos that Akhilesh posted- Mamata had earlier refused the visit Akhilesh was initially scheduled to visit Bengal on May 5, immediately after the election results were announced. However, Mamata reportedly asked him not to come at that time. Although Akhilesh did not campaign in the Bengal elections, he continued supporting Mamata through social media posts during the campaign period. First meeting after election defeat This was the first meeting between Mamata and any INDIA alliance leader after the Trinamool Congress defeat in the Bengal elections. Before this, Mamata and Akhilesh had last met on January 27. Political observers consider the renewed interaction between the Samajwadi Party and Trinamool Congress significant ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. 2 pictures of Mamata-Akhilesh meeting- TMC and DMK suffered major defeats In West Bengal, the BJP won 207 seats, while the Trinamool Congress was reduced to 80 seats. Compared with the 2021 elections, the BJP’s vote share increased by around 8%. Out of 119 seats that the TMC had consistently won for the past 15 years, the BJP captured 75 seats. This means the TMC lost nearly 63% of its traditional strongholds. Meanwhile, in Tamil Nadu, actor Vijay’s TVK secured 108 seats, while the DMK won 59 seats and the AIADMK secured 47. What does Akhilesh’s post indicate? Political analysts believe Akhilesh Yadav is trying to send a message of opposition unity by publicly standing with both Mamata Banerjee and MK Stalin. Senior journalist Rajendra Kumar said Akhilesh’s political style shows that once he aligns with someone, he generally avoids publicly attacking them, even after failed alliances. He pointed to the 2017 alliance between the Samajwadi Party and Congress, which performed poorly in elections. Despite the setback, Akhilesh did not make statements against Congress that could damage relations between the parties. The same pattern was seen after the 2019 alliance with Mayawati. Even after the alliance collapsed, Akhilesh refrained from criticising either Mayawati or the BSP. Rajendra Kumar added that Akhilesh’s restraint helped him gain support among Scheduled Caste voters. He also noted that even after the successful opposition alliance in the 2024 elections, several Congress leaders made controversial remarks against Akhilesh and the Samajwadi Party. Despite this, neither Akhilesh nor his party leaders responded aggressively. According to Rajendra Kumar, Akhilesh is attempting to project himself as a major opposition face who maintains cordial relations with all opposition parties, making him acceptable as a future national leader if such an opportunity arises.
