stories.title: Crack emerges in Taj Mahal’s historic Royal Gate:Stones fall from monument during storms and rain
stories.summary: The Taj Mahal, regarded as one of the most beautiful monuments in the world, is now showing visible signs of deterioration. The Royal Gate, also known as the Shahi Darwaza, has developed cracks in several places, while many stones have shifted from their original positions. The condition of the gate has become so fragile that it is no longer able to withstand storms and heavy rain. During recent spells of bad weather, stones from the structure broke off and fell twice. On several occasions, tourists narrowly escaped injury. This is not the first such incident. In recent years, stones, railings and jalis across different sections of the Taj Mahal complex have also collapsed or broken due to weakening structures and weather damage. Recent incidents at the Taj Mahal April 7, 2026- A powerful storm and heavy rain struck Agra. During the storm, white and red stones from the Royal Gate came loose and fell. Fortunately, no tourists were injured. April 30, 2026- Even a comparatively mild storm and rainfall proved too much for the weakened structure of the Royal Gate. Five pieces of white stone broke off and fell to the ground. Earlier incidents May 31, 2024- A stone from the Royal Gate broke and fell. December 20, 2024- Stones detached and fell from the wall of the Southern Gate of the Taj Mahal complex. May 29, 2020- Marble and red sandstone jalis in the Taj Mahal complex were damaged and broken. During the same incident, the Western Gate became tilted after one of its hinges broke. These incidents are only a few examples. Stones and lattice structures at the monument have reportedly broken and fallen multiple times over the years. Royal Gate in dilapidated condition The Royal Gate, considered the main entrance to the Taj Mahal, is now visibly deteriorating. Stones have loosened in several areas, while cracks can clearly be seen across sections of the walls. Many stones have weakened with age and are gradually detaching from the structure. The red sandstone gate also contains white and black stones used for decorative carvings, many of which are now falling out. In several places, gaps have formed in the walls where stones have collapsed. White and black decorative stones have also started coming loose from the structure. 4 pictures of the dilapidated Royal Gate- History of the Royal Gate The Royal Gate serves as the principal entrance to the Taj Mahal complex. After entering through the eastern or western gates, visitors reach the forecourt and then proceed to the main mausoleum through this gate. Earlier, tourists entering through the southern gate also approached the monument through the Royal Gate. However, the southern gate has remained closed since 2018. Historians believe the Royal Gate is as old as the main mausoleum itself and was constructed during the same phase of development. What historians and experts say ? Historian Rajkishore Raje said the Royal Gate was built alongside the main mausoleum during the Mughal era. At that time, it was known as the Shahi Darwaza. During British rule, it later came to be called the Royal Gate. SK Kulshrestha, former in-charge of the Taj Mahal and a retired Conservation Assistant with the Archaeological Survey of India, said the stones have naturally weakened with age. According to him, unless high-quality conservation work is carried out, stones will continue to crack and fall. He explained that conservation work was earlier handled directly by the department, with engineers carefully considering the monument’s historical characteristics. However, most restoration work is now contractor-driven. He believes contractors often lack the specialised expertise required for heritage conservation, which has affected the quality of repair work. Kulshrestha also pointed to the unavailability of traditional construction materials as a major concern. Earlier conservation work used pebble lime and specially prepared mortar containing strengthening compounds. Such materials are now difficult to obtain. Taj Mahal generates more than Rs 100 crore annually Despite repeated increases in ticket prices, tourist interest in the Taj Mahal remains extremely high. The monument continues to generate the highest revenue among sites protected by the Archaeological Survey of India. At present- An additional Rs 200 ticket is required to enter the main dome area. As a result, Indian visitors spend Rs 250 to view the complete monument, while foreign tourists pay Rs 1,300. Know the income for each year According to ASI data, offline ticket sales alone generated Rs 105 crore 49 lakh 12 thousand 855 during the financial years 2024-25 and 2025-26 combined. Including online ticket sales, the total revenue exceeded Rs 200 crore. Even after ticket prices increased over the decades, from just 20 paise to Rs 250 for Indian visitors, tourist numbers have not seen any major decline. Ticket system introduced in 1966 Entry to the Taj Mahal remained completely free until 1966. That year, a ticketing system was introduced for the first time, with tickets priced at just 20 paise. Today, a tiered pricing structure is followed to regulate the growing number of tourists, with separate rates for different categories of visitors. How ticket prices increased Concerns over conservation spending Concerns are also being raised over the amount spent on conservation compared with the monument’s earnings. Not only the Royal Gate, but several other sections of the Taj Mahal complex have also deteriorated over time. Stones continue to break and fall from various parts of the monument. Despite the monument generating hundreds of crores in revenue, ASI data shows that approximately Rs 5 crore was spent on conservation work at the Taj Mahal during the last financial year. Kalander Bind said that conservation work is being carried out regularly and that restoration projects worth around Rs 5 crore have been completed at the monument.

stories.title: Are police killings of child-crime suspects revealing a pattern?:UP witnesses three such shooting deaths in a month
stories.summary: On May 5 in Hardoi, a 7-year-old child was allegedly sexually assaulted and murdered, triggering outrage across Uttar Pradesh. Within 12 hours, police killed the accused, Mehnoor, in an encounter. The incident reflects a shifting pattern in UP Police action, where encounters are increasingly being used not only against mafia and crimes against women, but also against those accused of crimes against children. Know what kind of crimes the police were strict about earlier What is the latest pattern? Taking action on crimes against children within hours 4 recent major incidents show that the police are taking very aggressive action against those who commit crimes against children. How the Yogi government worked in 9 years Focus on organised crime After Yogi Adityanath became Chief Minister in 2017, curbing organised crime became a major focus. In the first 10 months of his government, UP Police carried out 1,142 encounters in which 34 criminals were killed. The first encounter was of Gurmeet in Saharanpur on March 31, 2017. Later, police killed Naushad and Sarwar in Shamli on July 29. Naushad had 19 serious criminal cases against him, while Sarwar had 8. Ikram was killed in an encounter on August 10, followed by Nadeem on September 8 and Shamshad on September 10. Cracked down on crimes against women 'Operation Langda' launched Police adopted a strategy of psychological pressure for those who molested or committed violence against women and daughters. Videos were released showing the accused with bandages on their legs (limping) and apologizing. This sent a message that those who molest or rape women will not be spared. 2019-21: Taught lessons to those who attacked the uniform Encounter for murder or assault of police 2024: Action on those who commit major robberies 25 encounters in one year 2025: Contract killers killed 48 encounters in 2025 This year, a maximum of 48 criminals were killed in encounters. Especially, contract killers were the target of UP Police. Among them, Banarasi Yadav of Varanasi was the main one. 24 cases were registered against him. More than half of these were for contract killings. UPSTF killed him in Chaubepur. Similarly, STF encountered Mohammad Rehan of Shamli, accused in 90 cases. Ashu alias Monty of Moradabad was considered a sharpshooter. STF and Moradabad Police killed him in an encounter. Read what Retired IPS Lalji Shukla says Question: When and how does the police pattern against crime change? Retired IPS: Police strategy changes with changing crime patterns. Around 20 years ago, organized crime and highway robberies were common. Later, criminals began looting families at gunpoint inside homes and even firing at police during encounters. Crimes against women and children are highly emotional issues, and public anger rises sharply in such cases. With CCTV cameras now common, incidents are often captured on video, increasing pressure on police to act quickly. As crime patterns evolve, police response also changes accordingly. Question: How can this model benefit the UP elections? Retired IPS: People want to feel safe and usually support governments that provide security. With elections approaching, the Yogi government will likely try to further strengthen this law-and-order image. The impact of UP model on the Bengal elections After BJP's victory in West Bengal, the 'UP Police Model' is in the headlines. PM Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah, and CM Yogi explained to the public during the campaign how the mafia rule was ended in UP. How were state borders secured? On this, Mamata Banerjee had to say that Bengal does not need any 'external model'. The agenda of Maa-Maati-Manush (Mother, Soil, People) is fine.

stories.title: Prayagraj murder case:Class 9 student Khushi’s skeletal remains gorged by animals, found in bush 17 days after murder
stories.summary: The carcass of a class nine student was found in a bushy area, 17 days after her murder, allegedly by her 17-year-old boyfriend in Prayagraj. Animals gorged on the skeletal remains of the rotten body. The family could find only her clothes and bones at the post-mortem house. Her mother, Sunita Pal, fainted upon seeing the body was in such a bad state. After regaining consciousness, she kept screaming. I want revenge. One life is gone, I want four lives in return. I want the lives of the killer, his family, and his maternal uncle. Khushboo, the elder sister of Khushi Pal, who was killed by her boyfriend, said, The murderer should be hanged. The entire family conspired to commit the murder. His family deserves the same. The boy's maternal uncle, maternal aunt, mother, and father are all involved in this murder. Khushi's sister Muskan said, We came to know about their affair a month ago. Our family had explained it to the boy. Then he told me to tell my sister to either choose him or choose the family. The person who killed my sister should receive the harshest possible punishment. Accused's family fled Since the arrest of the accused student, father Suresh Verma, mother Seema, and younger brother Apurva have been absconding. The house is locked. Relatives and neighbors living around the house cannot believe that a boy studying in intermediate can commit such a heinous murder. The accused's father Suresh, drives his own auto. Neighbor Sanjeev Verma said that the whole village knew he was a simple boy. No one thought he would commit murder. Sanjeev says he always kept to himself. He didn't talk much to people. Ria, named in the FIR When Khushi Pal ran away from home, her mother Sunita Pal named a girl named Ria Patel along with the lover. After the murder case came to light, the police also took Ria into custody. She was interrogated for a long time. Ria kept crying at the police station after being caught. Riya's important role in the love story Khushi's sister Khushboo says that Riya Patel is the accused's classmate. The accused introduced her to Khushi by making her his adopted sister. All conversations and meetings with Khushi happened through Riya. Khushi had saved Riya's number in her mobile. Friendship started on Instagram The distance between the ancestral homes of the accused and the girl is about 30 kilometers. Their friendship started on Instagram. Then they started looking for excuses to meet. In this crucial link, a house came in handy. Khushi's aunt's house is in Araipur Soraon. While the boy's maternal grandmother's house is right next door. Just by talking, both started living at their relatives' houses. They started meeting through their classmate Riya Patel. Khushi wanted to have a love marriage Both families were strict due to them being minors. Khushi wanted to have a love marriage. After this, she even talked to a relative who was a lawyer. Later, the boy's maternal uncle and others opposed it and stopped the matter. Understand the whole matter Khushi (17), daughter of auto driver Laxmi Narayan Pal, a resident of Jamunipur village, had an affair with a boy (17) from the Baharia area. Khushi was the second of 4 sisters. She studied in class 9 at Motilal Inter College in the same village. When both families came to know about their closeness, they explained to the children and asked them to stay away. When he didn't agree, the girl's family members also beat the young man. Meanwhile, Khushi kept pressuring him for marriage. To get rid of Khushi, the boy made a plan to murder her. He called Khushi to meet him during the day on April 20. Both decided that they would run away from home. According to the plan, the accused ran away from home with Khushi at night. Then, near the Sharda feeder canal, he stabbed her multiple times with a knife. He strangled her with a dupatta. Then he threw the body and fled.

stories.title: Rain and thunderstorm warning across 28 UP districts:Jalaun receives showers; temperatures drop, weather to change from tomorrow
stories.summary: The spell of storms and rain in UP has continued for the seventh straight day. On Friday morning, Jalaun witnessed rain and strong winds, with dark clouds covering the sky. Weather remained clear in Lucknow, Kanpur, Noida, and Ghaziabad, with bright sunshine and cooler conditions due to humidity, though temperatures are expected to rise later in the day. The Meteorological Department has issued a storm and rain alert for 28 districts, with lightning likely in some areas. The rain spell, ongoing since April 30, has brought major relief from heat, reducing maximum temperatures by up to 10°C. Banda, which recorded 47.6°C on April 28, saw temperatures fall to 38°C by May 7. On Thursday, rain lashed 15 districts, including Lucknow, Kanpur, and Barabanki, while Mahoba saw hailstorm and rain for nearly half an hour. In Bijnor, a CCTV tower collapsed during the storm. In Barabanki, slippery roads caused a collision involving several vehicles, including two double-decker buses, leaving one person dead. Jalaun in Bundelkhand recorded the state’s highest rainfall at 27 mm. Atul Kumar Singh, Senior Scientist at the Regional Meteorological Centre, Lucknow, stated: The active western disturbance of the past week is now weakening. Today, scattered rain may occur in eastern and western UP. There is a possibility of thunderstorms and lightning. From tomorrow, the heat will show its intensity. The mercury will start rising again. However, relief from heatwave will continue for now. Weather pictures Know the condition of the cities- Why are there weather fluctuations? The Meteorological Department says that the weather in the mountains of Uttarakhand is constantly changing. Snowfall is occurring. stories.title: UP cabinet expansion may reflect smart meter anger:AK Sharma could be shunted out of energy ministry
stories.summary: The UP government’s rollback on smart prepaid meters came amid rising public anger and growing anti-government sentiment. RSS and BJP leaders reportedly warned that not reversing the decision could hurt the party in the upcoming assembly elections. Now, high-level sources in the RSS and BJP say the Energy Department may be taken away from Energy Minister AK Sharma during the next cabinet expansion. 5 reasons for anger over smart prepaid meters 1. Postpaid meters converted to prepaid without consent: There are about 3.58 crore domestic electricity consumers in UP. By February 2026, smart meters were installed in 87 lakh of these homes. Of these, 82 lakh were smart postpaid meters. The department converted them into prepaid meters. This work started in January. After this, from March-April, the electricity department started disconnecting electricity connections for arrears. 2. Electricity disconnected for 5 lakh homes simultaneously: The real trouble started after this. The department disconnected electricity for more than 5 lakh homes simultaneously, citing a negative balance. Even after recharging, the supply did not resume. When people protested, the department clarified that it happened due to a technical issue. 3. Apprehensions regarding smart meters: Many videos went viral claiming that consumption was being recorded in smart prepaid meters even without an electricity connection. A common perception was formed that these meters run fast. The department could not dispel this notion. 4. No system for complaints: People complained that electricity bills were many times higher than the average. The department had no system to hear complaints. Complaints made on helpline 1912 were closed without resolution. 5. Net meters of solar plants removed: Even the net meters installed at the premises of consumers who had solar panels were replaced with smart prepaid meters. Then, their hefty bills were sent without deducting the electricity generated from solar. Understand how the decision to withdraw was made Public protests increased concern The BJP failed to gauge public anger over prepaid meters, while the SP and other opposition parties could not turn it into a political issue. As a result, people across UP united and protested on their own. Protests spread from Lucknow to Agra, Firozabad, Varanasi, Prayagraj, Hapur, Bareilly, and Mathura without any central leadership. Middle-class women even removed meters and protested outside electricity offices, with videos quickly going viral. As the issue escalated, CM Yogi Adityanath formed an expert committee to investigate smart meters. However, public anger continued, with fears it could fuel anti-incumbency against the government. Narrative was building against govt in election year A source associated with the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh says that despite widespread protests, the government did not want to withdraw its decision. Officials had convinced those in the government that people were protesting under the influence of some individuals. However, in the coordination meeting between the Sangh and the government, Sangh officials intervened. The Sangh said that the government should handle this matter as soon as possible. Meanwhile, the BJP organization was continuously receiving negative feedback from MLAs and BJP leaders regarding Energy Minister AK Sharma. Leaders from districts like Agra, Aligarh, Firozabad had made it clear that if the decision was not reversed, this issue would become a major problem in the elections. Opposition becoming active due to public protests Given the increasing protests across UP, political rhetoric had started from the Samajwadi Party (SP), Congress, and Aam Aadmi Party (AAP). Akhilesh Yadav had compared smart meters to EVMs. He had said- This is a big scam. Just as EVMs are not understood by people, smart meters are also a means of plunder. Akhilesh had even said that if the SP government is formed, 300 units of free electricity will be provided. After this, AAP's Rajya Sabha MP and UP in-charge Sanjay Singh had said- Smart meters are now looting the public by becoming 'smart cheaters'. Their speed has become faster than even Milkha Singh. Decision suddenly changed after results of 5 states On May 4, election results were announced in 5 states and union territories of the country. In West Bengal, TMC lost and BJP came to power for the first time. Seeing the changing equations, Energy Minister AK Sharma suddenly reached Shakti Bhawan on May 4 itself. After meeting with officials, he announced the abolition of the prepaid system. Now, consumers will again receive monthly bills. The facility to pay outstanding bills in installments has also been provided. The Energy Minister said - 'Consumer is God'. This decision has been taken considering technical difficulties and consumer complaints. Along with this, instructions were given that electricity should not be disconnected under any circumstances within one month. Smart meter flaws not rectified even in 3 years Energy Efficiency Services Limited (EESL), a Government of India company, had installed 1.2 million smart meters in UP in 2023. Even then, there was a lot of controversy surrounding it. Following this, the Government of India sent a high-level inquiry committee. The committee visited different parts of UP to understand the smart metering system, billing system, and consumer experience. Its report revealed several serious flaws related to smart meters. These have not been rectified even after 3 years.

stories.title: Govt issues order to convert prepaid meters to postpaid:Allows customers to pay power bills up to April in 10 installments
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has decided to convert prepaid smart electricity meters into postpaid meters. On Thursday, UP Power Corporation Managing Director Nitish Kumar issued instructions to all distribution divisions regarding the change. Following these directions, the electricity bill for May consumption, which will be issued in June, will now be on a postpaid basis. Bills will continue to be generated on the 10th of every month as usual. According to the corporation’s order, consumers will be allowed to pay the postpaid security deposit in four equal installments. Outstanding electricity dues can also be cleared in ten equal installments. The first installment of the security deposit must be paid in June along with the bill generated for May’s electricity usage. Consumers will receive their electricity bills through SMS and WhatsApp. Know what instructions were given in the order? Postpaid security amount will have to be paid in four installments According to the Chairman of Power Corporation, during the conversion to prepaid mode, the postpaid security amount was transferred to the balance. Now, due to switching back to postpaid, the security amount will have to be deposited in 4 installments as per the 'Cost Data Book-2026' and based on the sanctioned load. The first installment will have to be deposited with the bill to be issued in June. The other three installments will have to be deposited in the next three months. The RMS will issue this itself. Apart from this, as before, consumers will be given 15 days to deposit the bill. After this, a disconnection date of 7 days will be given. This will also be marked on the bill. As before, if any consumer is unable to deposit the bill by the due date, they will also have to pay a penalty. Outstanding bills till April can be deposited in 10 installments For the convenience of domestic consumers, the Power Corporation has provided the facility to deposit outstanding electricity bills in 10 installments along with a surcharge till 30th April. Consumers of other categories will have to deposit the outstanding amount in 3 installments in the ratio of 40%, 30%, 30%. Special camps from 15th May for bill complaints The Chairman has ordered all electricity companies to address the numerous complaints from people regarding outstanding bill amounts. For their resolution, special camps will be organized from 15th May to 30th June at the offices of all Executive Engineers and Sub-Divisional Officers. Apart from this, special arrangements are also being made for the 1912 helpline number. Why did the government have to discontinue the prepaid system? Electricity consumers say that smart meters run very fast. Due to this, higher bills are coming even with less usage. In fact, many times the balance decreases even without usage. As soon as the balance goes into minus, the electricity supply gets disconnected. Even after a recharge, the supply is often not restored immediately. On Sunday, protests regarding smart meters took place in Agra, Prayagraj, Kanpur, Lucknow, Fatehpur, and Varanasi. In Fatehpur, electricity consumers had uprooted smart meters and thrown them at the power house. In Agra, women uprooted smart meters from their homes and threw them on the streets. They said that we don't want smart meters, we want the old meters. After the installation of smart meters, electricity bills have been coming higher. Money is being deposited in advance. Even after depositing money, electricity is being cut. When inquired, they say that the balance is in minus.

This expansion, marked by recent victories in West Bengal and Odisha, transforms the party from a Hindi-heartland force into a dominant pan-India political machine, reflecting its governance model and increasing public acceptance.

stories.title: ‘Voters frustrated by slow pace of change’: Sadiq Khan ramps up pressure on Starmer after London poll setback
UAE to decide on remote or in-person classes on May 10 as schools and universities remain on alert
stories.summary: UAE schools and universities await a crucial May 10 announcement to determine the return to in-person learning or continued remote education. This decision follows a nationwide safety assessment prompted by renewed regional tensions and emergency alerts. Authorities are prioritizing student and staff safety while ensuring educational continuity.

stories.title: Has Mamata Banerjee accepted defeat? What her new X bio says
BJP says it will not support any party to form govt in TN
Indian sailor killed after dhow catches fire near Strait of Hormuz; 17 rescued
stories.summary: A fire aboard a wooden dhow near the Strait of Hormuz resulted in the death of one Indian sailor and injuries to four others. Seventeen Indian crew members were rescued by a passing vessel. The incident occurred amidst heightened regional tensions, with recent exchanges between Iran and the United States in the vital shipping lane.

stories.title: Arab Cinema shines at Cannes 2026 as Gulf Filmmakers lead major festival categories
stories.summary: Cannes 2026 highlights Arab and Middle Eastern cinema. Films from Palestine, Morocco, Egypt, and Iran feature prominently. This marks a shift towards culturally rooted storytelling. The festival emphasizes auteur cinema over Hollywood blockbusters. Arab filmmakers are gaining global recognition. This edition signifies a defining moment for regional cinema on the world stage.

stories.title: 'I bow to West Bengal Jana Shakti': PM Modi kowtows before Kolkata crowd as BJP forms first govt
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi expressed profound gratitude to the people of Bengal, bowing with folded hands after the BJP's historic Assembly election victory. Alongside new chief minister Adhikari, he shared an emotional moment with 98-year-old veteran Makhanlal Sarkar, even touching his feet in a gesture of deep respect. This marks a significant shift in West Bengal's political landscape.

stories.title: 'This is Punjab, not scared by threats': Bhagwant Mann after ED raid on minister
From Dilip Ghosh to Agnimitra Paul - what BJP’s first West Bengal cabinet looks like
stories.summary: Suvendu Adhikari took oath as the new Chief Minister of West Bengal. The BJP secured a significant win in the 2026 assembly elections. Several prominent leaders attended the swearing-in ceremony. The new government includes ministers like Dilip Ghosh, Agnimitra Paul, Ashok Kirtania, Kshudiram Tudu, and Nisith Pramanik. The state saw record voter turnout.

stories.title: Suvendu Adhikari takes oath as West Bengal's first BJP chief minister
stories.summary: Suvendu Adhikari has been sworn in as West Bengal's first BJP chief minister at a grand ceremony attended by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. This historic win, securing 207 seats, ends the Trinamool Congress' 15-year reign. Adhikari's transition from Mamata Banerjee's aide to BJP leader marks a significant political upheaval in the state, mirroring recent changes in Bihar.

stories.title: BJP’s ‘sonar’ era begins in West Bengal: Suvendu Adhikari takes oath as CM– top developments
stories.summary: West Bengal ushers in a new political era as Suvendu Adhikari takes oath as the state's first BJP Chief Minister. This historic win, following an overwhelming mandate, marks the saffron party's long-fought ideological battle. Adhikari's dramatic rise, from local councillor to defeating Mamata Banerjee, culminates in this significant power shift.

stories.title: More hunting, fewer limits: Trump lifts restrictions in national parks and wilderness areas
stories.summary: The Trump administration is expanding hunting and fishing access on federal lands, including national parks and wildlife refuges, by removing existing restrictions. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum stated the policy is to open lands unless specific exceptions apply. This move aims to boost conservation and rural economies, despite concerns about visitor safety and science-based management.

stories.title: 'Eternal voice of civilisation': PM Modi pays tribute to Rabindranath Tagore on 'pochishe boishakh'
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and West Bengal Chief Minister-elect Suvendu Adhikari paid tribute to Rabindranath Tagore on his birth anniversary, Pochishe Boishakh. Modi hailed Tagore as a timeless voice of Indian civilization, while Adhikari described him as an "eternal star" of Bengali literature. The occasion marks the Nobel laureate's enduring contributions to literature, philosophy, education, and culture.

stories.title: 'He was on the stairs': Iran claims Mojtaba Khamenei was knocked down by US blast but is 'recovering well'
stories.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is reportedly in good health, with officials dismissing rumors of severe injuries following recent strikes. While acknowledging minor wounds, they insist he remains active in state affairs. Meanwhile, the US awaits Iran's response to a proposal aimed at ending the West Asia conflict, with officials expressing hope for a serious offer.

stories.title: Inside a cave older than Egypt’s pyramids: 12,000-year-old stitched piece of elk hide may be the world’s oldest clothing
Backchannel deals, shifting loyalties and Vijay’s race for power - What’s unfolding in Tamil Nadu
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu's government formation remains uncertain as TVK emerges as the single largest party but falls short of a majority. Allies are scrambling for numbers, with some extending support while others withdraw, creating a volatile political landscape. Efforts are underway to secure the necessary support to stake a claim to power.

stories.title: TVK shares video of AMMK MLA writing support letter as Tamil Nadu govt suspense continues — Watch
AI tools to help centre catch fake Ayushman claims
stories.summary: New AI systems are now available to combat fraud in the Ayushman Bharat health insurance scheme. These advanced tools can identify fake hospital bills and forged medical documents. The technology aims to speed up insurance claim settlements and enhance transparency. India is leading the Global South with its health AI benchmarking platform.

stories.title: Two Indians in crew of hantavirus-hit ship
stories.summary: A rare hantavirus outbreak on a cruise ship with two Indian crew members has sparked international attention. Experts assure no immediate concern for India, citing previous sporadic cases. The Andes strain, linked to limited human-to-human spread, requires close exposure, unlike COVID-19. India's healthcare is prepared for potential cases.

stories.title: Lt Gen N S Raja Subramani appointed next CDS; Vice Adm Krishna Swaminathan to head Navy
YouTuber Ethan Klein caught screenshotting Anisa Jomha’s Instagram Story during live poker event as clip explodes online
stories.summary: A viral Celebrity Poker Tour clip showed Ethan Klein seemingly screenshotting Anisa Jomha’s Instagram Story during a livestream. The moment quickly spread online because of Ethan Klein’s past public feud with Ian “iDubbbz” Carter and earlier comments involving Anisa Jomha.

stories.title: “Danger to society”: Internet erupts after Mason Hull reportedly walks free despite charges involving minors
stories.summary: Mason Hull, popularly known as “Hullo,” was reportedly released on bond after being charged with 15 counts related to possession of explicit material involving minors. JiDion shared alleged jail records online and criticized Hull’s release, calling him a “danger to society.” The YouTuber also warned Sarasota residents to “be careful.” Hull has not publicly addressed the allegations or the growing backlash surrounding the case.

stories.title: SC acquits man after 22 years in jail, raps Delhi high court for nixing delayed appeal
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has ordered the release of a murder convict after 22 years, criticizing the Orissa High Court for dismissing his appeal solely on grounds of delay. The apex court invoked its extraordinary powers under Article 142, highlighting the convict's satisfactory jail conduct and lack of legal aid.

stories.title: TOI wins top honours at INMA awards
stories.summary: The Times of India secured top honors at the INMA awards in Berlin, winning first prize for "Thirukkural With The Times" in Best Use of Print (Regional) and third prize for "I am Kolkata, Amar Para" in Best Use of Social Media (Regional). The publication also received three honorary mentions for its reader engagement, video content, and revenue diversification strategies.

stories.title: “Stop destroying innocent lives”: Laura Loomer erupts at Candace Owens over Erika Kirk controversy
stories.summary: Laura Loomer publicly attacked Candace Owens for allegedly spreading conspiracy theories about the death of Charlie Kirk and targeting his widow, Erika Kirk. Loomer called Owens a “modern-day cult leader” and accused her of “destroying innocent people’s lives.” Erika Kirk also pleaded with Owens to stop discussing her family. The feud has since escalated with accusations involving lawsuits, doxxing, and attacks on Owens’ husband, George Farmer.

stories.title: We’re extremely shy of ordering arrest, says SC on ADAG probe
stories.summary: The Supreme Court emphasized its reluctance to direct arrests, prioritizing evidence collection and witness protection. While monitoring investigations, the bench declined to comment on the merits of the Anil Ambani Group (ADAG) case, citing past collateral damage to reputations. The CBI has filed nine FIRs totaling Rs 27,337 crore against ADAG entities.

stories.title: Rs 7,000 GPS watches for Haj pilgrims not working
stories.summary: Indian Haj pilgrims are questioning a mandatory Rs 7,000 GPS smartwatch, part of a Rs 10,000 airfare hike. Many devices, procured by the Haj Committee and supplied by Sekyo Innovations, reportedly fail to turn on or track pilgrims, causing distress, especially for the elderly. This initiative, aimed at safety, faces criticism over cost and execution.

stories.title: Huntington's patients seek rare disease tag & registry
stories.summary: Families and researchers are advocating for Huntington's disease to be recognized as a rare disease in India to establish a much-needed registry. This recognition is crucial for quantifying patient numbers, improving treatment accessibility, and securing coverage under national health policies, offering hope for affected individuals and families.

stories.title: Shashi Tharoor moves Delhi high court to block AI deepfakes
stories.summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor has approached the Delhi High Court seeking protection against AI-generated deepfake videos depicting him praising Pakistan and discussing sensitive political matters. He argued that such content could harm India's international standing and be exploited by foreign entities.

stories.title: Supreme Court in no mood to condone Madhya Pradesh minister in Col Sofiya Qureshi case
stories.summary: The Supreme Court expressed strong disapproval of Madhya Pradesh minister Kunwar Vijay Shah's controversial remarks, questioning the state government's decision on prosecuting him. Despite the Solicitor General suggesting the minister intended praise, the bench noted a lack of repentance and the statement's unfortunate impact. The court also directed the SIT to investigate other instances of the minister's objectionable statements.

stories.title: Illegal infiltration into India not terror act: Supreme Court; gives bail to Bangladeshi who helped others to cross over
stories.summary: The Supreme Court stated that illegal infiltration by Bangladeshi nationals is not a terrorist act, even as the BJP vows to expel them from West Bengal. The court granted bail to an individual arrested for facilitating illegal immigration, noting the porous border with Bangladesh and the large number of immigrants already in India.

stories.title: Bengal's Adhikari: Suvendu to be state's first BJP CM
Kolkata: Writers' buildings to turn saffron to welcome new CM
stories.summary: Kolkata's iconic Writers' Buildings and other government offices will glow orange on Saturday evening, marking the first day of the new BJP government. Illumination trials were conducted Friday. The historic Writers' facade, along with Assembly House and Kolkata Collectorate, will be lit up. Inside, preparations are underway for the new Chief Minister's symbolic visit.

stories.title: Kolkata: Brigade takes rain cover for new cabinet swearing-in
stories.summary: Preparations are in full swing at Kolkata's Brigade Parade Ground to ensure Saturday's oath-taking ceremony for Bengal's first BJP government proceeds smoothly despite heavy rains. A massive waterproof hangar tent has been erected, and seating capacity has been significantly increased. Authorities are working round-the-clock to restore the grounds, with an indoor stadium on standby as a backup.

stories.title: Satheesan backers stage protests, Kerala Congress leadership steps in
stories.summary: Congress leadership intervened as supporters of opposition leader V D Satheesan held demonstrations across Kerala, demanding his appointment as the next chief minister. Some activists allegedly tore down posters of AICC leader K C Venugopal, also a contender for the post, prompting the KPCC to direct workers to refrain from such actions.

stories.title: Hunt for killers of Suvendu's aide expands to UP, Odisha
stories.summary: Bengal CM-designate Suvendu Adhikari's aide Chandranath Rath's murder probe now includes contract killers from UP and Odisha. Sleuths are focusing on Montu Mondal, who was in the SUV during the attack and escaped. A car used in the crime was traced to a Matigara owner who'd advertised it for sale online.

stories.title: Voter support or MLAs' backing? Congress weighs its options in Kerala
stories.summary: Congress leadership is deliberating on the Kerala CM post, weighing intra-party support for KC Venugopal against public sentiment favoring VD Satheesan. A decision is expected by Sunday, with discussions involving key state leaders and central party chiefs in Delhi.

stories.title: Can't sit next to Congress in Lok Sabha anymore, DMK tells Speaker
Twitch CEO Dan Clancy announces stricter action against viewbotting
stories.summary: Twitch is implementing a new system to combat viewbotting, a practice where streamers artificially inflate viewer numbers. Starting in May, repeat offenders will face concurrent viewership caps based on their real traffic, with penalties escalating for persistent violations. The platform aims to create a fairer environment for legitimate creators by addressing fake engagement.

stories.title: West Bengal victory will plug national security hole: Amit Shah
stories.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah declared the BJP's West Bengal victory a national security triumph, promising to identify and remove infiltrators. He criticized the TMC for political violence and criminalization, vowing a new era of fearless governance and dismantling the 'syndicate raj'.

stories.title: ‘Four feet tall, wearing space suits and helmets’: FBI UFO files reveal bizarre claims
Tamil Nadu CM announcement: Governor cannot question majority stitched post-poll
stories.summary: Supreme Court rulings consistently state governors must invite the largest party or alliance to form government post-election, without questioning how support was gained. The apex court has warned against dismissing governments or dissolving assemblies based on 'fanciful assumptions' of horse-trading, emphasizing that majority must be proven on the floor of the House.

stories.title: How drama in Tamil Nadu unfolded, the several plots, offers of friendship & a 'betrayal'
stories.summary: Following TVK's electoral success, AIADMK factions engaged in backroom dealings to form a government, with one group attempting to ally with TVK while the party's general secretary sought a tie-up with DMK. These maneuvers ultimately failed as Left parties opted to support TVK, thwarting the Dravidian majors' plans.

stories.title: Element of surprise key to secure strategic edge, Rajnath tells commanders
stories.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh emphasized that future wars will hinge on innovative thinking and synergy, not just weaponry. He urged commanders to prioritize artificial intelligence, autonomous systems, and secure communications, stressing the need to anticipate enemy surprises and stay ahead. Singh highlighted hybrid threats and multi-domain operations, commending the forces' jointness and technological adoption.

stories.title: 62-year-old Indian-American man to be denaturalized for $2.5 million fraud, false information
Supreme Court turns down scamster's plea to club FIRs
stories.summary: The Supreme Court refused to consolidate multiple FIRs against Sameer Agrawal, accused of defrauding thousands of investors of Rs 10,000 crore and fleeing to Dubai. The court emphasized a victim-centric approach, stating that each instance of cheating warrants an independent FIR. It suggested considering consolidation only if duped investors collectively petitioned, and if Agrawal deposits the full refund amount.

stories.title: In a 1st, NCRB tracks cases of cruelty against animals: 10,312 arrested in 2024
stories.summary: For the first time, the National Crime Records Bureau has tracked animal cruelty cases, registering 9,039 incidents and arresting over 10,000 individuals in 2024. Maharashtra led with the highest number of cases. The data reveals a high conviction rate for concluded cases but significant delays in judicial disposal.

stories.title: Murder, abetment accused can't inherit victim's property: Supreme Court
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has ruled that individuals accused of murder or abetting murder cannot inherit property from their victims. This disqualification applies to both wills and intestate succession, even if a trial is ongoing. The court emphasized that no one should profit from their own wrongdoing, citing principles of justice and public policy.

stories.title: India gets new labour law as govt notifies wage code; Centre caps weekly working hours at 48 under new labour codes
stories.summary: New labour codes have capped weekly working hours at 48, with overtime paid at double the hourly wage. Final rules for wages and industrial relations codes are out, paving the way for implementation. A National Reskilling Fund will support retrenched workers with new skills, financed by employers.

stories.title: Patna-bound IndiGo flight makes emergency landing at Lucknow due to bad weather
stories.summary: An IndiGo flight from Kolkata to Patna made an emergency landing in Lucknow due to adverse weather conditions in Patna. The aircraft, carrying 180 passengers and six crew members, was diverted after being unable to receive landing clearance. The flight later departed for Patna once the weather improved.

stories.title: Texas woman running for Governor mocks Indians, says her new name is 'Pria'
'Suspension of all kinetic activity': Trump announces 3-day Russia-Ukraine ceasefire, 1,000-prisoner swap
stories.summary: US President Trump announced a three-day Russia-Ukraine ceasefire from May 9-11, hoping for a long-term peace deal and a prisoner exchange. Despite this, fighting persisted, with both sides reporting attacks. Ukraine accused Russia of continuing assaults, while Russia claimed to intercept numerous drones. The truce follows Russia's Victory Day, a proposal Kyiv had previously dismissed.

stories.title: Quote of the day by James Watson: “Worrying about complications before ruling out the possibility that the answer was simple would have been damned foolishness.”
‘CIA knew Iran would shut down Hormuz...’: Ex-counterterror chief makes bombshell claim
SIT files charge-sheet against man accused of bid on Farooq Abdullah’s life
stories.summary: A charge-sheet has been filed by the SIT against Kamal Singh Jamwal, 63, for the attempted assassination of former J&K CM Farooq Abdullah. Jamwal allegedly fired at Abdullah during a wedding ceremony in Jammu, driven by resentment over Kashmiri migrant issues. The SIT's investigation indicates a pre-meditated intent to target the politician.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Queen Victoria: “Then, dear Mamma, I hope you will grant me the first request I make to you, as Queen. Let me be by myself for an hour.”
'Is the fight for Green Card worth it?' H-1B visa holder says he has decent money but can see parents once every two years
Old major NH bridges to get smart sensors for early warning alerts
stories.summary: Highway authorities will now install advanced sensors on old major bridges across National Highways for continuous health monitoring. This initiative aims to detect abnormal behavior early, enabling prompt corrective actions and preventing potential mishaps. The system will be operational for at least 10 years after installation.

stories.title: 'I’d rather die in my country': Why immigrants are leaving voluntarily instead of detention
10K women 50+ category: Strength, spirit, and the joy of running | Times Internet Half Marathon
10,312 arrested in 2024 in cases linked to cruelty against animals, NCRB tracks animal cruelty cases for first time
stories.summary: For the first time, the NCRB has compiled data on animal cruelty, registering 9,039 cases and arresting over 10,000 individuals nationwide in 2024. Maharashtra leads with the highest number of reported incidents. This comprehensive data offers a crucial statistical overview of how animal cruelty offenses are managed within India's legal framework.

stories.title: 10K male 50+ category: Runners who showed the magic of experience| Times Internet Half Marathon
Details Of Prison Killing: Prosecutors outline Ian Watkins attack; UK inmates face murder charge
stories.summary: Rico Gedel allegedly stabbed former Welsh singer Ian Watkins to death in HMP Wakefield with a homemade blade, boasting about his "fame" afterward. Prosecutors claim Gedel and Samuel Dodsworth planned the attack, with CCTV showing Gedel entering Watkins' cell shortly before the stabbing. Watkins, serving time for child sex offenses, had faced prior threats.

stories.title: Passenger from 'Hanta virus' cruise visited school on remotest island Tristan de Cunha, believed to be infected
Decoding Bengal SIR data: Of 123 margins, 49 in closer focus
stories.summary: West Bengal's election saw a political earthquake, with BJP's massive win overshadowing concerns about Special Intensive Revision (SIR). Analysis reveals voter deletions exceeded winning margins in numerous seats, particularly in areas with significant supplementary deletions. While some seats showed clear BJP gains, others indicated TMC erosion without a direct BJP benefit, highlighting complex local dynamics.

stories.title: Rangasamy meets LG, stakes claim to form government in Puducherry
stories.summary: Rangasamy, who has been the longest-serving chief minister of Puducherry, presented a letter of support from the legislative assembly members demanding the right to form the government. The letter has been sent for the President's approval.

stories.title: Glow hard: Trump's nuclear threat grows darker in face of Iranian defiance
Suvendu Adhikari's swearing in: Date, time, and guest list as West Bengal gets its first BJP CM
Elon Musk’s DOGE mass cancellation of grants based on race and gender criticised by US judge
US town mayor fires entire police department for upsetting his wife, says he won't block paychecks
Amazon begins drone deliveries in UK with Darlington pilot programme
Kash Patel orders lie detector tests for FBI staff to identify who questioned his leadership
‘I wouldn’t pay it either’: Donald Trump slams sky-high World Cup ticket prices that fans must pay to attend
stories.summary: Donald Trump has joined growing criticism over soaring 2026 FIFA World Cup ticket prices, admitting he would not personally pay $1,000 to watch the United States national team play. As resale values continue spiralling and supporters raise affordability concerns, FIFA president Gianni Infantino continues defending the tournament’s controversial pricing model.

stories.title: Hindutva mascot, ex-TMC insider: 5 reasons why BJP chose Suvendu Adhikari as West Bengal CM
stories.summary: Suvendu Adhikari emerged as the BJP's choice for West Bengal Chief Minister after years of being the party's strongest anti-Mamata Banerjee face. His victories, including defeating Banerjee in her stronghold, solidified his position. Adhikari's insider knowledge of the TMC and ability to consolidate Hindu votes made him the natural leader for the BJP's first government in the state.

stories.title: Ahmedabad Air India crash: Minister says probe in final stage, report expected next month
26-year-old Indian student dies of heart attack in US, a day after celebrating graduation walk
Evening news wrap: Suvendu Adhikari to become West Bengal CM; TVK's Vijay gets majority in Tamil Nadu & more
TCS Nashik sexual harassment case: Key accused remanded in police custody till May 11
‘Enough is enough’: SC raps MP govt over delay in action against minister Vijay Shah over remarks on Col Sofiya Qureshi
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has strongly criticized the Madhya Pradesh government for delaying the decision on sanctioning prosecution for minister Kunwar Vijay Shah's "most unfortunate" remarks against Army officer Sofiya Qureshi. The court has ordered the state to comply with its earlier directive within four weeks, emphasizing that "enough is enough."

stories.title: South America’s Champions League match stopped less than 2 mins in after fans started burning stadium sections
stories.summary: Chaos engulfed a Copa Libertadores clash between CR Flamengo and Independiente Medellín after violent fan protests forced the match to be abandoned minutes after kick-off. Fires, pitch invasion attempts and attacks on journalists highlighted deep unrest surrounding Medellín’s ownership, with Flamengo now expected to receive a 3-0 victory under CONMEBOL regulations.

stories.title: West Bengal after Northeast and Bihar: BJP's 'outsider leader' model in difficult states
Operation Sindoor: How close India and Pakistan came to the brink one year ago
stories.summary: Following a deadly terror attack in Kashmir, India launched precision strikes on militant camps in Pakistan, escalating tensions to a full military standoff. Despite Pakistan's nuclear threats, India maintained a strong stance, ultimately leading to a ceasefire after significant damage to Pakistani military assets.

stories.title: Suvendu Adhikari: Ex-Mamata loyalist, who defeated her twice, to be Bengal's 1st BJP CM
stories.summary: Suvendu Adhikari comes from one of the state’s most influential political families. His father, Sisir Adhikari, served both in the West Bengal Assembly and the Lok Sabha, while his brother Dibyendu Adhikari was earlier a Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP before joining the BJP in 2024. Suvendu began his political journey with the Congress during the 1995 municipal polls before moving to the newly formed TMC alongside his father in 1998. He rose rapidly within Mamata Banerjee’s party and became one of its strongest organisational faces in coastal Bengal.

stories.title: BJP government formation in West Bengal: Suvendu Adhikari elected as legislature party leader, set to take oath as CM on May 9
stories.summary: Senior BJP leader Suvendu Adhikari has been formally elected as the leader of the BJP legislature party in West Bengal. This development paves the way for him to become the state's first BJP chief minister. The swearing-in ceremony is scheduled for May 9 at Brigade Parade Ground in Kolkata.

stories.title: 'Premature and misplaced’: Sanjay Raut writes to Trump over Bengal win message to PM Modi; BJP hits back
stories.summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut criticized Donald Trump's congratulations to PM Modi on the West Bengal election results, calling them premature and misplaced. Raut asserted that state elections are an internal matter and alleged the polls were conducted amid fear and systemic pressure, questioning the Election Commission's impartiality.

stories.title: Kerala CM face: BJP drops leaked Congress list with 'KC' markings
stories.summary: With the LDF's victory in Kerala, the race for Chief Minister heats up. A leaked list, shared by the BJP, suggests K C Venugopal might be favored by a majority of Congress MLAs. However, one MLA claims his preference was omitted, raising questions about the consultation process. V D Satheesan and Ramesh Chennithala are also contenders.

stories.title: The Vijay question: Should governor ascertain majority before inviting govt formation?
stories.summary: Actor-politician Vijay's TVK party emerged as the single-largest force in Tamil Nadu, winning 108 seats. Despite this, Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar has paused an invitation to form the government, citing an "unestablished majority." This has triggered a constitutional showdown, with legal experts debating the governor's discretionary powers and the necessity of a floor test before an invitation.

stories.title: Hantavirus scare on cruise ship: Two infected Indians asymptomatic; ICMR says no immediate threat to India
stories.summary: Two Indian nationals aboard a cruise ship have tested positive for hantavirus, but health officials assure there's no immediate threat to India. The virus, primarily spread by rodents, does not transmit easily between humans. Global health authorities are monitoring the situation, with the public risk deemed very low.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu government formation: Vijay passes first political test with 118 marks - how TVK got the numbers
Is Vinícius Júnior leaving Real Madrid? Crisis deepens amid training-ground fight and player hospitalisation
stories.summary: Vinícius Júnior is at the centre of fresh uncertainty at Real Madrid CF, with reports linking him to Premier League interest as contract talks stall and his current deal enters its final stretch. Despite strong performances this season, the Brazil forward’s future is now in question, adding further tension at a club already dealing with internal instability ahead of El Clásico.

stories.title: UK’s ‘first gay dad’ Barrie Drewitt-Barlow and husband charged with rape, sex trafficking

Quote of the day by Carl Jung: “Loneliness does not come from having no people about one, but from being unable to communicate the things that seem important to oneself, or from holding certain views which others find inadmissible.”
'Changed political circumstances': Kanimozhi writes to Lok Sabha speaker seeking separate seating for DMK MPs after break-up with Congress
stories.summary: DMK MP Kanimozhi has requested Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla to change parliamentary seating arrangements, moving DMK MPs away from Congress. This follows the end of their two-decade alliance in Tamil Nadu after the recent poll results. The DMK accused Congress of betrayal for supporting another party to form the government, warning of widespread electoral consequences.

stories.title: Message for Congress? Akhilesh shares Mamata, Stalin photos with cryptic 'not ones who abandon' post
stories.summary: Akhilesh's remark was in the backdrop of the Congress snapping ties with ally DMK in Tamil Nadu and extending support to actor Vijay's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), which has added to rancour in the INDIA bloc. The 2026 assembly elections in Tamil Nadu and West Bengal have cast a foreboding shadow on the NDA's rival bloc as Mamata and Stalin were two powerful regional leaders in the anti-BJP camp.

stories.title: 'Reply and let us know': VCK attacks Vijay's 'arrogance' over WhatsApp outreach amid Tamil Nadu govt crisis
stories.summary: Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi (VCK) criticizes actor-politician Vijay's TVK for seeking government support via WhatsApp messages instead of direct consultations. VCK questions Vijay's political handling and accuses his party of misguiding him and exploiting his popularity while also criticizing TVK's stance on dynastic politics and resort politics.

stories.title: 'Political stupidity': Mani Shankar Aiyar questions Congress for backing TVK without ensuring majority
How black holes become cosmic monsters: Scientists uncover the violent merger chain behind giant space objects
Most expensive ticket ever? World Cup final seat listed for $11.5 million despite being one of the worst in stadium
stories.summary: A standard ticket for the 2026 FIFA World Cup final at FIFA World Cup 2026 Final has appeared on the resale market for an extraordinary $11.5 million, despite offering no premium benefits. The pricing surge at MetLife Stadium highlights escalating concerns over affordability and speculation, as global demand for the expanded tournament intensifies ahead of its North American showcase.

stories.title: ‘Who will trust us again?’ Mani Shankar Aiyar tears into Congress-TVK alliance gamble in Tamil Nadu
108 seats but no majority: Can TVK's Vijay form govt? Tamil Nadu number game explained
Explainer: Can hantavirus outbreak become Covid 2.0?
stories.summary: Health authorities are urgently tracing passengers from the MV Hondius cruise ship following a hantavirus outbreak that has claimed three lives. The Andes strain, capable of human-to-human transmission, was identified, prompting isolation and contact tracing. While not comparable to COVID-19, the virus requires close contact to spread.

stories.title: Sir David Attenborough celebrates 100th birthday: The life, legacy, and global impact of the world’s most beloved natural history broadcaster
British fashion brand co-founder James Holder jailed for 8 years for rape after Cheltenham night out
Real Madrid in crisis? Valverde ruled out of El Clásico ahead of Barça clash after training-ground fight
stories.summary: Federico Valverde has been ruled out of El Clásico after suffering a head injury during a reported training-ground altercation with teammate Aurélien Tchouaméni, deepening the crisis inside Real Madrid CF. With dressing-room tensions escalating, scrutiny surrounding Kylian Mbappé intensifying, and pressure mounting on manager Álvaro Arbeloa, Madrid head into their decisive clash against FC Barcelona amid growing instability.

stories.title: Vijay under pressure, DMK-AIADMK scramble to stop TVK from forming govt: Tamil Nadu post-poll chaos explained in 10 points
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu's political landscape shifted dramatically as Vijay's TVK emerged as the largest party, winning 108 seats but falling short of a majority. Intense negotiations followed, with Congress backing TVK, causing friction with the DMK. stories.summary: A suspected hantavirus outbreak aboard the luxury expedition ship MV Hondius has resulted in three deaths and several serious illnesses, prompting an international health response. The virus, typically spread by rodents, has raised concerns due to its rapid escalation and potential for severe respiratory complications. Authorities are working to contain the crisis and evacuate affected passengers.

Who is Charles Lieber? Convicted Harvard scientist now leading China’s research to link the brain with computers

His move to i-BRAIN, a key institute, highlights China's focus on this medically promising yet strategically sensitive field, drawing global attention to his new role.

Mamata Banerjee vs Suvendu Adhikari: TMC leading in Bhabanipur in trends
stories.summary: West Bengal's high-stakes political battle intensifies as Mamata Banerjee and Suvendu Adhikari face off in Bhabanipur. While Banerjee has a strong history in the constituency, a significant number of Muslim voters are under scrutiny, potentially impacting the TMC's victory margin.

stories.title: Rape-murder of 3-year-old: Kin seek death, protest shuts down Pune district
stories.summary: A brutal rape and murder of a three-year-old girl has sparked outrage in Pune's Bhor-Rajgad belt, leading to a shutdown. The victim's family refuses to meet politicians until the 65-year-old accused, a repeat offender, is sentenced to death. Protests erupted, with the Chief Minister assuring a fast-track trial and pursuit of the death penalty, while cautioning against public execution demands.

stories.title: Israel issues evacuation warning; kills 1, hurts 4 in Lebanon strikes
stories.summary: Israeli airstrikes in southern Lebanon claimed at least one life and injured four rescuers on Sunday, despite a fragile truce. The Lebanese health ministry condemned the attacks, citing violations of the Geneva Convention. Israel issued new evacuation warnings for over ten villages, including those north of the Litani River, as tensions escalate following threats from Israel's military chief.

stories.title: Crowdfunding helps Serbian birdwatchers save woodland
stories.summary: A Serbian bird society successfully crowdfunded 8,000 euros to purchase and protect a two-hectare woodland, preventing its likely deforestation. This initiative highlights growing public concern for environmental protection in Serbia, a nation grappling with pollution and development threats. The society aims to preserve the 'Nightingale's Forest' and inspire similar local conservation efforts.

stories.title: Middle East crisis: Iran proposes 30-day plan to end war, says it has received US reply
stories.summary: Iran has received a US response to its 30-day peace proposal, conveyed via Pakistan. The offer aims to end the ongoing war, not just extend a ceasefire, and suggests delaying nuclear talks until after hostilities cease. The US President expressed doubt about the proposal's success, citing Iran's past actions.

stories.title: Tensions intensify at Strait: Cargo ship sailing near Hormuz attacked by Iran
stories.summary: A bulk carrier was attacked by small craft near Iran's coast in the Strait of Hormuz, with all crew reported safe and no environmental impact. This incident occurs amidst heightened tensions as the US enforces a counter-blockade on Iranian ports and plans to guide ships through the strait, drawing a strong warning from Tehran.

stories.title: Abetment case filed in Delhi judge’s death
More Strait talks: Trump rolls out 'Project Freedom' to guide ships through Hormuz
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump launched 'Project Freedom' to aid commercial ships stranded in the Strait of Hormuz, citing humanitarian concerns and low supplies. He stated the US will guide vessels safely out, emphasizing these ships belong to nations uninvolved in regional disputes. Trump also revealed positive discussions with Iran, though he rejected their latest proposal for conflict resolution.

stories.title: Congress: Government ignored Nicobar concerns
stories.summary: Congress has challenged the government's Great Nicobar Project, asserting that local communities and environmentalists' serious concerns remain unaddressed. Citing a former naval chief, the party questioned linking security with the development plan, which includes a township and tourist infrastructure. Congress also highlighted the Nicobarese community's withdrawal of its No Objection Certificate, emphasizing the island's unique ecosystem.

stories.title: Heart donated in Panchkula gives Sudanese teen in Delhi new life
stories.summary: A 14-year-old Sudanese boy received a life-saving heart transplant in Delhi, thanks to a donor heart flown from Haryana. The organ came from a 41-year-old woman declared brain dead, whose family bravely consented to donation.

stories.title: Abandoned in forest, 2-year-old walks for 20 hours, survives
stories.summary: A two-year-old boy miraculously survived nearly 20 hours alone in a wild animal-infested forest after his father allegedly murdered his mother and abandoned him. Found weak and dehydrated by police, the toddler's incredible resilience in the face of extreme danger has stunned authorities. The father has been arrested, and the child is recovering.

stories.title: Team Raghav Chadha to get audience with President Murmu ahead of Bhagwant Mann
stories.summary: Punjab's political landscape is heating up as rival factions, led by AAP MP Raghav Chadha and CM Bhagwant Mann, are set to meet the President. The dispute centers on alleged defections and police actions, with Chadha planning to highlight a "political vendetta" following FIRs against fellow MP Sandeep Pathak. BJP has also voiced concerns over alleged retaliation.

stories.title: Canadian intelligence agency accuses India of interference, spying
stories.summary: Canada's intelligence agency has listed India and China among nations involved in foreign interference. While acknowledging historical covert actions by India, the report highlights Khalistan extremism as a significant national security threat to Canada. This comes amid efforts to mend ties between Ottawa and New Delhi, with the latest report notably downplaying previous accusations against India.

stories.title: India dismisses Nepal’s Kailash yatra objection over Lipulekh Pass
stories.summary: Nepal has officially objected to India resuming the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra through Lipulekh Pass, a territory it claims based on the 1816 Sugauli Treaty. India dismissed these claims as unjustified and historically unfounded, stating Lipulekh has been a long-standing yatra route. This dispute marks a potential test for bilateral ties as both nations prepare for diplomatic discussions.

stories.title: 'Brown kids' comment was out of love: Michigan democrat El-Sayed says JD Vance is 'deeply evil' though
SG Tushar Mehta takes swipe at ‘bully’ judges in his book
stories.summary: Senior advocate Tushar Mehta's upcoming book criticizes some judges for exhibiting 'judicial bullying' due to excessive courtroom reverence. He argues that while judges face immense pressure, this cannot justify incivility, as the public expects high standards from an institution they cannot easily remove. Mehta highlights the power imbalance lawyers face when confronting arrogant judges.

stories.title: NASA scientists reveal a 2.5-billion-year-old hidden structure within the Great Dyke of Zimbabwe
Bengal SIR a ‘threat’ to our jobs: Professionals, government staff move court

Professionals, including a PSU officer, teacher, doctor, and insurance agent, have moved the Calcutta High Court, fearing their citizenship will be questioned, potentially leading to job termination and licence cancellation. Their appeals for urgent hearings were denied.

stories.title: I am one of Brij Bhushan's six victims, reveals wrestler Vinesh Phogat
stories.summary: Wrestler Vinesh Phogat revealed she is one of six accusers of former WFI chief Brij Bhushan Singh. Her return to competition in his stronghold, Gonda, raises concerns about fairness and potential bias in officiating. Phogat, now a legislator, demands transparency, holding the government accountable for any incidents. The WFI president assures safety and denies bias.

This innovative spacecraft combines optical and radar imaging, enabling it to 'see' through clouds and darkness, offering crucial capabilities for national security and disaster response.

stories.title: Nepal stirs row with India, objects to Kailash Mansarovar yatra via Lipulekh
stories.summary: Nepal has objected to India and China's plan to conduct the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra via Lipulekh Pass, asserting the territory belongs to Nepal based on the 1816 Treaty of Sugauli. Kathmandu stated it was not consulted and has conveyed its position to both nations, urging them to cease activities in the disputed region.

stories.title: Brixton Drive-By Shooting Probe: Four men hurt in moving-car attack; police hunt suspects
stories.summary: Four people were injured in a shooting from a moving car in Brixton shortly after midnight on Saturday. A 25-year-old man is in critical condition, while three others sustained non-life-threatening injuries. Police are conducting an intensive investigation, reviewing CCTV and gathering witness statements to identify the suspects responsible for this act of indiscriminate violence.

stories.title: Assembly elections 2026: From East to South, key battlegrounds to watch out for
stories.summary: After the counting begins and trends trickle in, these seats offer early clues to momentum, alliance cohesion and voter sentiment that can ripple across regions. From prestige contests involving chief ministers to urban battlegrounds testing new entrants, the outcomes in these constituencies will help explain whether incumbency holds or fractures. They also reflect how local issues such as welfare delivery, identity, urban infrastructure and leadership credibility interact with wider political narratives.

stories.title: ‘He is a mouse': TMC's Kunal Ghosh slams 'Singham' cop Ajay Pal Sharma over repolling in Falta, demands suspension
stories.summary: Following serious accusations of election fraud in West Bengal's Falta area, Trinamool Congress heavyweight Kunal Ghosh is demanding that the controversial IPS officer, Ajay Pal Sharma, popularly known as 'Singham', be suspended. Ghosh believes Sharma's actions are directly linked to the alleged rigging that has cast a shadow over the election results.

Experts suspect a chemical compound, possibly with industrial origins, contaminated the burn, causing significant ecological and economic damage during the peak fishing season.

Chief minister MK Stalin remains the central figure in the state’s political battle, and governance credit is expected to accrue largely to his party. For Congress, which continues as a junior partner in the alliance, such an outcome would ensure representation and continuity, but not necessarily greater political ownership.

stories.summary: As vote counting looms for five key states, the 2026 assembly elections represent a critical juncture for national parties and regional strongholds. The ruling NDA, led by AINRC, faces a strong challenge from the Congress-led SPA and emerging player TVK. Key constituencies like Thattanchavady and Mannadipet are closely watched.

stories.title: Laugh in the face of darkness: How humor became humanity's oldest coping mechanism
stories.summary: Amidst hardship, dark humor emerges as a vital survival tool, offering a defiant spark against despair. This article explores how gallows humor, distinct from denial, helps individuals and communities cope with overwhelming realities. It highlights Gen Z's use of memes as a modern form of crisis comedy, underscoring laughter's profound psychological and biological benefits.

stories.title: J&K: Heavy landslide shuts Baramulla-Uri NH near Lagama; traffic diverted
stories.summary: Heavy landslides have blocked key routes in Jammu and Kashmir. The Baramulla-Uri highway faced disruption near Lagama, with traffic diverted. The Doda-Kishtwar road also saw a major blockage near Gatsoo. Meanwhile, a bridge collapse in Jammu's Bantalab area tragically claimed the lives of three labourers. Authorities are working to clear debris and ensure safety.

stories.title: 'Not surprising': BJP MP Sandeep Pathak on 2 FIRs filed against him, says he has no information on cases
stories.summary: Rajya Sabha MP Sandeep Pathak stated he has not received information about FIRs filed against him, suspecting political misuse. Punjab Police registered two non-bailable FIRs against Pathak after he switched from AAP to BJP. BJP and SAD leaders condemned the actions as political vendetta.

stories.title: "Erika pointing a gun at Charlie's neck": Candace Owens quietly edits controversial AI-generated Erika Kirk thumbnail amid online outrage
stories.summary: Candace Owens is facing renewed backlash after quietly editing a controversial thumbnail linked to her latest episode. Critics claim the changes were subtle and failed to address the core issue, while supporters continue to defend her intent. The episode was also renamed and added to a series, raising further questions. The controversy has grown alongside reports of legal action against conspiracy-driven content tied to Erika Kirk and Charlie Kirk.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu assembly elections: From MK Stalin to EPS and Vijay; key candidates to watch on May 4
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu's political landscape is set for a decisive turn as vote counting commences. The election features high-stakes contests, including Chief Minister MK Stalin defending his seat and actor-turned-politician Thalapathy Vijay making his electoral debut. AIADMK leader Edappadi K Palanisami is also fighting to regain relevance, with new entrants and alliance dynamics shaping the traditional voting patterns.

stories.title: Diljit Dosanjh halts Canada show midway, slams fans waving pro-Khalistan flags 'jinne jhande dikhane dilkhai challo'
stories.summary: Diljit Dosanjh paused his Calgary concert amid pro-Khalistan flags, addressing criticism. This follows past controversy with Sikhs For Justice over his interactions with Amitabh Bachchan.

In contrast, the LDF is largely seen falling short, with projections indicating a ceiling below a simple majority. If these projections hold, the outcome would carry significance beyond a routine change of government.

stories.title: 'MPs who switched to BJP targeted': Raghav Chadha accuses Punjab govt of political vendetta, to meet President Droupadi Murmu on May 5
stories.summary: Rajya Sabha MP Raghav Chadha is set to meet President Droupadi Murmu on May 5 to voice concerns regarding the alleged misuse of state machinery in Punjab. He plans to highlight political vendetta against former AAP MPs who recently joined the BJP. Chadha, along with three other MPs, will present these issues to the President.

Voter list controversies also mark this crucial election.
